instruction:
Create the API interface specification for an e-commerce shopping mall platform with the following requirements.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

I want to create an e-commerce shopping mall platform.

## Customer Account

- This platform requires registration to use any features (no guest browsing)
- Customers sign up with email and password
- Customers log in with email and password
- Customers can change their password
- Customers can delete their account
- When a customer deletes their account:
  - Their profile information is deleted
  - Their orders and order history are preserved (for seller records and legal purposes)
  - Their reviews are preserved but shown as "deleted user"

## Customer Profile

- Each customer has a profile with: display name and phone number
- Customers can edit their display name and phone number

## Address Management

- Customers can add multiple shipping addresses
- Each address has: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country
- Customers can edit their addresses
- Customers can delete their addresses
- Customers can set one address as the default shipping address

## Seller Account

- Sellers sign up with email and password
- Sellers log in with email and password
- Sellers can change their password
- Seller accounts require administrator approval before they can sell
- Sellers can view their approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- If rejected, sellers can view the rejection reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Sellers can delete their account only if:
  - They have no pending orders (paid or shipped status)
  - They have no pending cancellation or refund requests
- When a seller deletes their account:
  - Their products are deleted from listings
  - Order history and snapshots are preserved
  - Their shop name in past orders is preserved

## Seller Profile

- Each seller has a profile with: shop name, shop description, and logo image
- Sellers can edit their shop name, description, and logo
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can view seller profiles

## Categories

- Products are organized into categories
- Categories can have subcategories (one level of nesting only)
- Each category has: name and description
- Categories are created and managed by administrators only
- Customers can browse the list of all categories
- Customers can view products within a category

## Snapshot Principle

- This is a platform where money is exchanged, so all data modifications must be recorded
- Whenever editable data is modified, a snapshot is created to preserve the previous state
- Snapshots record: when the change was made, what was changed, and the values before and after
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Snapshots can be viewed by relevant parties (owners, administrators) for dispute resolution

**Product Snapshot Structure**
- When a product is edited, a product snapshot is created
- The product snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category, base price, images)
- The product snapshot also includes snapshots of all variants at that moment (product-snapshot → product-snapshot-SKU)
- This preserves the complete state of a product and its variants at any point in time

**Snapshot applies to:**
- Products (all fields including images)
- Product variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Seller profiles (shop name, description, logo)
- Order items (product, variant, and seller profile at time of purchase)
- Reviews (rating, text content)
- Cancellation requests (reason, status changes)
- Refund requests (reason, status changes)

## Products

- Sellers can create products
- Every product has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (required)
  - Category (required, can select a subcategory)
  - Base price (required)
- Products belong to the seller who created them
- Sellers can edit their own products
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete their own products only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for any variant of the product
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant of the product
- Deleting a product also deletes all its variants and inventory records
- Deleted products no longer appear in search or category listings
- Sellers can view snapshots of their own products
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Snapshots are preserved even after product deletion

## Product Images

- Sellers can upload multiple images for each product
- Images can be reordered (first image is the main/thumbnail image)
- Sellers can delete images from their products
- Image changes are included in product snapshots

## Product Variants (SKU)

- A product can have multiple variants
- Each variant represents a specific combination of options (e.g., "Red / Large", "Blue / Small")
- Each variant has:
  - SKU code (unique identifier, required)
  - Option values (e.g., color: "Red", size: "Large")
  - Price (can override the base price, optional)
  - Stock quantity (required, starts at 0)
- Sellers can add variants to their products
- Sellers can edit variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Every variant edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete variants only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for that variant
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for that variant
- A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable
- Products with no variants are visible in search but shown as "unavailable"

## Inventory Management

- Each variant has its own stock quantity
- Stock quantity is managed through inventory history records (not snapshots)
- Each inventory record contains: quantity change (positive for restocking, negative for orders/adjustments), reason, and timestamp
- Current stock is calculated by summing all inventory records
- Sellers can add inventory (restock) with a quantity and reason
- Sellers can subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with a quantity and reason
- Order placement automatically creates a negative inventory record
- Order cancellation/refund automatically creates a positive inventory record
- Sellers can view the full inventory history of each variant
- When stock reaches 0, the variant is shown as "out of stock"
- Out of stock variants cannot be added to cart

## Product Search

- Customers can search products by name
- Search results show products from all sellers
- Search results are paginated
- Customers can filter search results by:
  - Category
  - Price range (minimum and maximum)
  - In-stock only
- Customers can sort search results by:
  - Newest first
  - Price (low to high)
  - Price (high to low)

## Product Listing

- When viewing a list of products (search results, category page), each product shows:
  - Main image (thumbnail)
  - Name
  - Base price (or price range if variants have different prices)
  - Seller shop name
  - Average rating (if reviews exist)

## Product Detail Page

- Customers can view a single product's full details
- The page shows:
  - All images
  - Name and description
  - Category
  - Seller shop name (links to seller profile)
  - All available variants with prices and stock status
  - Average rating and total review count
  - All reviews

## Wishlist

- Customers can add products to their wishlist
- Customers can view their wishlist
- The wishlist is paginated
- Wishlist shows products (not specific variants)
- Customers can remove products from their wishlist
- If a product is deleted by the seller, it is automatically removed from all wishlists

## Shopping Cart

- Customers can add variants to their cart (must select a specific variant, not just a product)
- When adding to cart, customers specify the quantity
- If the same variant is already in the cart, the quantities are combined (not added as a separate line)
- Customers can view their cart
- Cart shows each item with: product name, variant options, price, quantity, and subtotal
- Customers can change the quantity of items in their cart
- Customers can remove items from their cart
- Cart shows the total price of all items
- If a variant's stock is less than the cart quantity, a warning is shown
- If a variant is deleted or out of stock, it is marked as unavailable in the cart

## Checkout

- Customers can proceed to checkout from their cart
- Unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Customers must select a shipping address (or use default)
- Customers can review the order summary before placing the order:
  - List of items with prices
  - Shipping address
  - Total price
- Once an order is placed, the shipping address cannot be changed

## Payment

- After reviewing, customers confirm and place the order
- Payment is processed (assume external payment gateway integration)
- Payment can succeed or fail
- If payment fails, the order is not created and customers can retry
- If payment succeeds, the order is created

## Order Creation

- When an order is placed successfully:
  - Stock quantities are decreased for each purchased variant
  - Items are removed from the customer's cart
  - An order record is created
  - Each purchased variant becomes an order item with status "paid"
  - A snapshot of each purchased product and variant is saved with the order item (preserves product name, description, variant options, and price at the time of purchase)
  - A snapshot of each seller's profile is saved with the order item (preserves shop name and logo at the time of purchase)

## Order Structure

- An order contains one or more order items
- Each order item represents a purchased product variant with a quantity
- If a customer buys 3 of the same variant, it becomes one order item with quantity 3
- Order items can be from different sellers
- Each order item has its own status
- Each order item can be individually cancelled or refunded
- Order items are grouped into shipments when shipped (see Shipping and Tracking)

## Order History

- Customers can view a list of all their orders
- The list is paginated and sorted by newest first
- Each order in the list shows: order number, date, total price, and overall order status
- Customers can view the full details of an order:
  - List of items with: product name, variant, quantity, price, and item status
  - Shipping address
  - List of shipments with tracking information (each shipment shows which items are included)

## Order Status

**Order Item Status**
- Each item in an order has its own status
- Item statuses:
  - Paid: payment completed, waiting for seller to ship
  - Shipped: seller has shipped the item
  - Delivered: item has been delivered
  - Cancelled: item was cancelled
  - Refunded: item was refunded

**Order Status**
- The overall order status is derived from its items
- If all items are paid → order is "paid"
- If any item is shipped (and none delivered yet) → order is "shipped"
- If all items are delivered → order is "delivered"
- If all items are cancelled → order is "cancelled"
- If all items are refunded → order is "refunded"
- Mixed states (e.g., some delivered, some refunded) → order is "partially completed"

## Shipping and Tracking

**Shipment Concept**
- A shipment is a package sent by a seller
- A shipment can contain one or more order items from the same seller
- Different sellers always ship separately (different shipments)
- A seller can choose to ship items individually or bundle multiple items into one shipment

**Shipping Process**
- Sellers can view order items for their products that need shipping
- When shipping, sellers select one or more of their items to include in a shipment
- Sellers enter tracking information for the shipment (carrier name, tracking number)
- All items in the same shipment share the same tracking information
- When a shipment is created, all items in it change to status "shipped"

**Delivery Confirmation**
- Customers can view tracking information for each shipment
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment (not per item)
- When the customer confirms delivery, all items in that shipment change to status "delivered"
- If the customer does not confirm, items automatically change to "delivered" after 14 days from shipping

## Order Cancellation

- Cancellation is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request cancellation for individual items with status "paid" (not yet shipped)
- Cancellation requests include a reason (text)
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the cancellation request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is cancelled and refund is processed for that item only
- Cancelled items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order continue processing normally
- If all items in an order are cancelled, the entire order status becomes "cancelled"

## Refund Requests

- Refund is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request a refund for individual items with status "delivered"
- Refund requests include a reason (text)
- Refund can be requested within 7 days of that item being delivered
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the refund request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is refunded
- Refunded items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order are unaffected
- If all items in an order are refunded, the entire order status becomes "refunded"

## Reviews and Ratings

- Customers can write a review for products they have purchased
- A review can only be written after that item's status is "delivered"
- Customers can write one review per product per order
- Each review has:
  - Rating (1 to 5 stars, required)
  - Text content (optional)
- Reviews are displayed on the product detail page
- Reviews are sorted by newest first
- Customers can edit their own reviews
- Every review edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can delete their own reviews (but snapshots are preserved)
- Product's average rating is calculated from all non-deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard

- Sellers can view a summary of their shop:
  - Total number of products
  - Total number of order items (for their products)
  - Number of pending cancellation requests
  - Number of pending refund requests
- Sellers can view a list of all order items for their products
- Sellers can filter order items by status

## Administrator System

**Becoming an Administrator**
- Any user (customer or seller) can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

**Administrator Grades**
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

**Seller Management**
- Administrators can view the list of pending seller approvals
- Administrators can approve or reject seller registrations
- When rejecting, administrators must provide a reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Administrators can suspend seller accounts
- When a seller is suspended:
  - Their products are hidden from search and category listings
  - Their products cannot be purchased
  - They can still process existing orders (ship items, respond to cancellation/refund requests)
  - They cannot create new products or edit existing products
- Administrators can unsuspend seller accounts (products become visible again)

**Category Management**
- Administrators can create categories and subcategories
- Administrators can edit category names and descriptions
- Administrators can delete categories (products in deleted categories become uncategorized)

**Product Oversight**
- Administrators can view all products on the platform
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Administrators can delete any product (for policy violations)

**Order Oversight**
- Administrators can view all orders on the platform
- Administrators can force-cancel individual items or entire orders (refunds the customer, restores stock)
- Administrators can force-refund individual items or entire orders

**User Management**
- Administrators can view all customer accounts
- Administrators can ban customers (banned customers cannot log in)
- Administrators can unban customers
- Administrators can view all seller accounts
- Administrators can ban sellers (banned sellers cannot log in, existing orders remain)

operations.specification: Create a customer account by validating the submitted email and password against the customer registration rules, ensuring the email is unique in mall_platform_customers and that the password meets the platform's credential policy. On success, create the customer record and any required session/auth state in a single transactional flow, then return freshly issued access and refresh tokens in the authorized response. Reject duplicate emails, invalid credential formats, and any persistence failures with appropriate 4xx or 5xx errors.
operations.description:
Register a new customer account and issue authentication tokens.

This operation creates a new customer identity in the marketplace so the user can access customer features that require authentication. The submitted email and password are used to create the account, and the system returns token credentials for immediate sign-in.

The account is stored in the customer actor table, and the resulting authentication state is returned as an authorized payload. Duplicate email addresses and invalid credential values are rejected to preserve account uniqueness and security.

Use this endpoint as the first step in the customer authentication workflow before accessing shopping, order, wishlist, cart, or profile features.

requestBody.description: Customer registration credentials used to create a new account.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens issued after successful customer registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Validate the submitted email and password against mall_platform_customers. Confirm that the account exists, is active, and is not blocked by account status rules before issuing new tokens. If the credentials are invalid or the account is disabled, return an authentication error without revealing which part failed. On success, create or rotate the customer session/auth state as required by the token service and return the new authorized payload.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing customer and issue tokens.

This operation verifies the customer's email and password and returns authentication tokens for accessing customer-only features. It is the standard sign-in entry point for shopper accounts.

The login flow should respect account status controls stored in the customer table, including blocked or otherwise ineligible accounts. The response contains the authorized authentication payload used by the client to continue the session.

Use this endpoint together with registration and refresh to manage the customer authentication lifecycle.

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials used to authenticate an existing account.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens issued after successful customer login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate the provided refresh token for the customer session flow, confirm it is not expired or revoked, and issue a new access token pair. The operation should bind the token to the customer session records in mall_platform_customer_sessions as needed by the implementation. If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or does not belong to the customer, return an authorization error and do not issue new tokens.
operations.description:
Renew a customer's authentication tokens.

This operation exchanges a valid refresh token for a new authorized token set so the customer can remain signed in without re-entering credentials. It supports the stateless JWT authentication lifecycle for shopper accounts.

The refresh flow depends on the customer session records used by the authentication system. Invalid, expired, or revoked tokens are rejected to prevent session misuse.

Use this endpoint when the client needs to silently continue a customer session after access token expiration.

requestBody.description: Customer refresh token payload used to renew authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens issued after successful token refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Validate seller registration credentials, create the seller account record, and return a newly issued authenticated token set. The service must reject duplicate emails, malformed passwords, and any account state that makes registration invalid. Registration should not depend on approval workflow state beyond creating the seller identity; seller approval is handled by separate business processes.
operations.description:
Register a new seller account with email and password.

This operation creates the seller's authentication identity for the marketplace and starts the merchant onboarding flow. It returns the standard authorized token response immediately after a successful registration so the seller can continue into seller-specific features.

The server must validate credential format and uniqueness before creating the account. If the email is already in use or the payload is invalid, the operation fails with a client error.

The response uses the platform's standard authorized format for authenticated seller access.

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller response containing the issued tokens for the newly registered account.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Verify seller login credentials against the stored seller account data and issue a fresh authenticated token set on success. Reject unknown emails, invalid passwords, banned accounts, and any seller account that is not eligible to sign in according to current moderation state. Keep authentication failures generic to avoid revealing whether the account exists.
operations.description:
Sign in an existing seller account with email and password.

This operation validates seller credentials and returns the authenticated token pair used for subsequent seller API calls. It is intended for merchants who already have an account and need access to seller operations such as product management, inventory updates, order processing, and shop profile management.

If the seller account is banned or otherwise not permitted to sign in, the operation fails even when the credentials are correct. Invalid credentials also fail with an authentication error.

On success, the response provides the seller's authorization data in the standard authorized format used across the platform.

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller response containing the issued tokens for the signed-in account.

This operation keeps an authenticated seller session alive without requiring the seller to re-enter their password. It uses the seller session and account state to determine whether the refresh token is still valid and whether the seller is still eligible to access the platform.

Expired, revoked, malformed, or account-mismatched refresh tokens are rejected. If the seller account can no longer sign in because of account status restrictions, token renewal fails as well.

When successful, the operation returns a new authorized response so the seller can continue using authenticated endpoints without interruption.

operations.specification: Validate the submitted email and password against mall_platform_customers. Confirm that the account exists, is active, and is not blocked by account status rules before issuing new tokens. If the credentials are invalid or the account is disabled, return an authentication error without revealing which part failed. On success, create or rotate the customer session/auth state as required by the token service and return the new authorized payload.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing customer and issue tokens.

This operation verifies the customer's email and password and returns authentication tokens for accessing customer-only features. It is the standard sign-in entry point for shopper accounts.

The login flow should respect account status controls stored in the customer table, including blocked or otherwise ineligible accounts. The response contains the authorized authentication payload used by the client to continue the session.

Use this endpoint together with registration and refresh to manage the customer authentication lifecycle.

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials used to authenticate an existing account.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens issued after successful customer login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate the provided refresh token for the customer session flow, confirm it is not expired or revoked, and issue a new access token pair. The operation should bind the token to the customer session records in mall_platform_customer_sessions as needed by the implementation. If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or does not belong to the customer, return an authorization error and do not issue new tokens.
operations.description:
Renew a customer's authentication tokens.

This operation exchanges a valid refresh token for a new authorized token set so the customer can remain signed in without re-entering credentials. It supports the stateless JWT authentication lifecycle for shopper accounts.

The refresh flow depends on the customer session records used by the authentication system. Invalid, expired, or revoked tokens are rejected to prevent session misuse.

Use this endpoint when the client needs to silently continue a customer session after access token expiration.

requestBody.description: Customer refresh token payload used to renew authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens issued after successful token refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Validate seller registration credentials, create the seller account record, and return a newly issued authenticated token set. The service must reject duplicate emails, malformed passwords, and any account state that makes registration invalid. Registration should not depend on approval workflow state beyond creating the seller identity; seller approval is handled by separate business processes.
operations.description:
Register a new seller account with email and password.

This operation creates the seller's authentication identity for the marketplace and starts the merchant onboarding flow. It returns the standard authorized token response immediately after a successful registration so the seller can continue into seller-specific features.

The server must validate credential format and uniqueness before creating the account. If the email is already in use or the payload is invalid, the operation fails with a client error.

The response uses the platform's standard authorized format for authenticated seller access.

requestBody.description: Seller registration payload containing the credentials required to create a new seller account.

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller response containing the issued tokens for the newly registered account.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Verify seller login credentials against the stored seller account data and issue a fresh authenticated token set on success. Reject unknown emails, invalid passwords, banned accounts, and any seller account that is not eligible to sign in according to current moderation state. Keep authentication failures generic to avoid revealing whether the account exists.
operations.description:
Sign in an existing seller account with email and password.

This operation validates seller credentials and returns the authenticated token pair used for subsequent seller API calls. It is intended for merchants who already have an account and need access to seller operations such as product management, inventory updates, order processing, and shop profile management.

If the seller account is banned or otherwise not permitted to sign in, the operation fails even when the credentials are correct. Invalid credentials also fail with an authentication error.

On success, the response provides the seller's authorization data in the standard authorized format used across the platform.

requestBody.description: Seller login payload containing the credentials required to authenticate an existing seller account.

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller response containing the issued tokens for the signed-in account.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate the seller refresh token, confirm that it belongs to an active seller session, and issue renewed tokens according to the platform's token rotation policy. Reject expired, revoked, malformed, or account-mismatched refresh tokens. If the seller account has been banned or otherwise invalidated, token renewal must fail even if the token is otherwise structurally valid.
operations.description:
Renew the seller's authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This operation keeps an authenticated seller session alive without requiring the seller to re-enter their password. It uses the seller session and account state to determine whether the refresh token is still valid and whether the seller is still eligible to access the platform.

Expired, revoked, malformed, or account-mismatched refresh tokens are rejected. If the seller account can no longer sign in because of account status restrictions, token renewal fails as well.

When successful, the operation returns a new authorized response so the seller can continue using authenticated endpoints without interruption.

requestBody.description: Seller refresh payload containing the refresh token used to obtain a new authenticated session.

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller response containing the refreshed tokens for the active seller session.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Implement administrator registration by validating the submitted credentials, ensuring the administrator identifier is unique, storing the password as a secure hash, and creating a new administrator account record when registration is permitted. After successful creation, issue the standard authorization tokens and return them in the authorized payload. Reject duplicate identifiers, malformed input, and any account-creation policy violations without creating partial records.
operations.description:
Register a new administrator account and return authorization tokens.

This endpoint creates an administrator sign-in account from the submitted registration credentials and returns the standard authorized payload after successful account creation. It is the entry point for provisioning a new privileged administrator identity in the mall platform.

The request must satisfy the administrator registration rules, and the response contains the authorized token set used by the application after sign-up. If the account already exists or the submitted data is invalid, the request is rejected without creating a partial account record.

requestBody.description: Administrator registration credentials used to create a new administrator account.

responseBody.description: Authenticated administrator token payload returned after successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implement administrator login by locating the administrator account using the submitted identifier, verifying the password against the stored hash, and confirming the account is eligible to sign in. Reject banned, suspended, or otherwise restricted administrator accounts according to account status rules. On success, issue a new authorization token payload and return it to the client. Use a generic authentication failure response for invalid credentials to avoid account enumeration.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing administrator account and return authorization tokens.

This endpoint validates administrator credentials against the stored account record and issues a new authorized token set when the credentials are correct. It is the standard sign-in operation for the administrator actor.

If the identifier or password is invalid, or if the administrator account is not allowed to sign in, the request is rejected. Successful authentication returns the standard authorized DTO used throughout the mall platform authentication flow.

requestBody.description: Administrator sign-in credentials used to validate the account and create an authenticated session.

responseBody.description: Authenticated administrator token payload returned after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implement administrator token refresh by validating the submitted refresh token, confirming that it belongs to a valid administrator session, and issuing a new token pair. Reject expired, revoked, malformed, or mismatched refresh tokens. Rotate the refresh token if the session policy requires it, and preserve the administrator identity and claims in the newly issued authorization payload. Do not accept access tokens in place of refresh tokens.
operations.description:
Refresh an administrator's authentication tokens.

This endpoint exchanges a valid administrator refresh token for a new authorized token payload. It is used to continue an authenticated session without requiring the administrator to log in again.

The request is rejected when the refresh token is expired, invalid, revoked, or not associated with a valid administrator session. A successful refresh returns the standard authorized DTO for the administrator actor.

requestBody.description: Administrator refresh-token request used to obtain a new authorized token payload.

responseBody.description: Refreshed administrator token payload returned after successful token renewal.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Search and list customer accounts with pagination and filtering.

This endpoint provides a paginated customer account directory for administrative browsing and user management. It is intended for finding registered customers by account criteria such as status or identity-related search terms, while keeping authentication credentials and session data out of the response.

The result set should respect the requested pagination and sorting options, and empty searches should return an empty page rather than an error. This operation supports platform oversight workflows only and does not permit anonymous access to customer data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the mall_platform_customers table as a paginated search endpoint.
Apply filtering and sorting from the request body against customer account fields that are available in the schema, and return summary rows only.
Do not include passwords, reset tokens, or session records in the response.
Use stable pagination ordering so repeated searches with the same criteria yield consistent results.
If no customers match the filters, return an empty page.
If the request contains invalid pagination or unsupported filter values, reject it before running the query.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of customer account summaries for administrative browsing.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering, sorting, and paginating customer accounts.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single customer account and its current profile information.

This endpoint returns the customer account identified by customerId together with the associated customer profile when one exists. It is intended for account detail views and administrative inspection workflows, and it must not include unrelated customer-owned resources such as carts, wishlists, orders, addresses, or sessions.

The service must confirm that the target customer account exists and that the caller is allowed to view it under the platform's access rules. If the account cannot be found, return a not-found error. If the caller lacks permission, return a forbidden error. If the profile row is absent because it was removed or has not been created yet, return the customer account data without fabricating profile fields.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the customer account by its UUID primary identifier and, if present, join the related customer profile in the same read path. Treat this as a read-only lookup: do not mutate any tables and do not assemble data from other customer-owned aggregates.

Use mall_platform_customers as the primary source and mall_platform_customer_profiles as the optional related source. Return only actual stored fields from those schemas. If the profile does not exist, the account should still be returned. If the customer does not exist, return not found. Enforce authorization according to actor rules so regular customers can only view their own account while administrators may inspect customer accounts according to moderation policy.

responseBody.description: The customer account details and associated profile information, if present.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the customer account to retrieve (UUID).
parameters.name: customerId

operations.description:
Update the signed-in customer’s profile information.

This operation updates only the current customer profile for the authenticated account. The profile stores the customer’s display name and phone number, which are used across the shopping experience for presentation and contact.

The submitted profile data is validated before persistence. Incomplete or unsuitable values are rejected, and the existing profile remains unchanged when validation fails. If the profile no longer exists because the account was deleted or the record is otherwise unavailable, the request is rejected instead of creating a new profile.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the authenticated customer from the current session, then fetch the associated row from mall_platform_customer_profiles. Enforce ownership so the caller can update only their own profile record.

Validate both display name and phone number before saving changes. Reject requests with missing, empty, or otherwise unsuitable profile values. Do not modify customer credentials, shipping addresses, orders, or any unrelated tables.

Update the existing profile row only. If the profile record is missing, return an unavailable/not-found response and do not recreate it. If the platform later creates snapshot history for customer profile edits, generate that snapshot only after a successful database update.

responseBody.description: The updated customer profile returned after the changes are saved successfully.

requestBody.description: The profile fields to update for the authenticated customer. Only customer identity and contact information may be changed.

operations.description:
Search and list authenticated sessions with pagination and filtering.

This operation returns session records in a paginated form so callers can inspect login activity and manage active access. It is intended for account security and operational review, not for authentication itself.

The result is limited to the caller's permitted scope. Customers may only view their own customer sessions, sellers may only view their own seller sessions, and administrators may only view sessions they are authorized to inspect. The response never includes sensitive session secrets or password reset material, and an empty result page is returned when no sessions match the criteria.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the session persistence tables for the current actor type and apply the request-body filters, pagination, and sorting. Return summary rows only; do not expose session tokens, password reset credentials, or other secret material.

Enforce strict authorization by actor scope. A customer must only receive their own customer sessions, a seller must only receive their own seller sessions, and an administrator must only receive sessions allowed by platform policy. If the request targets an unauthorized scope, return an authorization error rather than leaking session existence. Keep the implementation read-only and avoid any side effects on session state.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summaries matching the requested filters and visibility scope.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, pagination settings, and sorting options for listing authenticated sessions.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summaries matching the requested filters and visibility scope.

operations.description:
Returns a single authentication session record.

This endpoint is used to inspect one active or historical session entry, including the owning account reference, client context captured at creation time, and the expiration timestamp that determines whether the session is still valid.

Access is limited to the owning signed-in account or to administrators when the platform authorization rules permit session review. If the session does not exist, belongs to another account without permission, or is otherwise inaccessible under account status rules, the request must fail with an appropriate not-found or forbidden response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Look up the session by its UUID primary key and return the record only when the requester is authorized to inspect it. Use the current authenticated actor context to verify ownership or administrator-level access before exposing any data.

Return the session fields defined by the underlying session schema: id, owner foreign key, ip, href, referrer, created_at, and expired_at. Do not modify the session. If the row is missing, return not found. If access is denied, return forbidden. If the runtime session belongs to a different actor type than the current context and policy does not allow cross-actor inspection, treat it as inaccessible.

responseBody.description: The requested authentication session record.

parameters.description: The session identifier (global UUID).
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Resets an account password using a valid recovery token.

This operation is part of the account recovery flow and applies only when the provided reset token exists, has not expired, and matches a valid customer, seller, or administrator account reset record. The new password becomes the account’s future login credential after the reset succeeds.

The server must validate the token before updating any credential data. If the token is invalid, expired, or already used, the request must be rejected and no password data should be changed. The operation should also reject requests that fail password policy validation or do not match the account associated with the token.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Look up the password reset record by the submitted token and verify it is still valid and not expired. Determine the target account type from the token’s associated reset record, then update the corresponding account password hash in a transaction. Invalidate or consume the reset token after a successful update so it cannot be reused.

Validate the new password against the platform’s password policy before writing anything. If validation fails, return an appropriate client error and do not modify the account or reset record. If the token cannot be found, is expired, or is otherwise unusable, return a not-found or conflict-style error as appropriate and do not change persisted data.

Because this endpoint is used for recovery, it must not require the caller to be already authenticated. It should apply the same token handling rules across customer, seller, and administrator password reset tables, using the reset token to identify which table and account record to update.

requestBody.description: Password reset submission containing the recovery token and the new password to apply to the matching account.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single password reset record by its identifier.

This endpoint returns the stored reset request information used for account recovery workflows. It is read-only and does not consume the token, update the expiration, or change any account credentials.

The service should return a not-found error when the requested reset record does not exist. If access to the reset record is restricted by account ownership or internal authorization rules, the service should reject unauthorized requests with a permission error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the password reset record matching the provided resetId from the appropriate password reset table for the account scope in use. Perform a direct primary-key lookup and return the stored record unchanged. Do not modify token state, expiration metadata, or any related account record.

If the record is missing, return a 404-style error. If the authenticated principal is not allowed to inspect the reset record, return a 403-style error. Keep the endpoint fully read-only so it can be used safely by recovery or administrative inspection flows.

responseBody.description: The password reset record requested by identifier.

parameters.description: The password reset record identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: resetId

operations.description:
Search and page through seller accounts.

This operation returns a paginated list of seller summaries for administrative review and platform browsing use cases. It is intended for filtering by seller state and related search criteria, not for retrieving a single seller record.

The response contains summary data only, so clients can render list screens without loading the full seller account entity. Results should respect the current seller lifecycle state and any access-control rules applied by the service layer, including unavailable states such as banned or otherwise restricted accounts.

Validation and error handling should reject malformed pagination or filter input, and return a not-found style error only when the requested page or scoped data cannot be resolved by the service logic.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the mall_platform_sellers collection with pagination, search, and sorting. Apply the request body criteria to filter by seller account state and any supported textual search fields exposed by the seller listing use case. Sort deterministically and return a paginated result set of seller summaries.

The implementation should not expose password credentials or session data. Include only list-safe fields from the seller account and any directly related summary data needed for browsing. If seller approval status or availability is represented in related tables, join only the fields needed for list presentation. Ensure unavailable seller states are handled according to business rules, and do not silently include records that the current actor is not permitted to see.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of seller summaries suitable for administrative or platform list screens.

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for seller list browsing.

operations.description:
Retrieve a seller account and its linked shop profile by seller ID.

This endpoint returns the seller’s current account state together with the public shop information owned by that seller account. It is suitable for seller profile pages, administrative review screens, and other detail views that need the seller’s approval status and rejection reason when present.

The seller account is identified by its UUID primary key. The response should reflect the current live seller account record and the associated seller profile if it exists. If the seller account cannot be found, return a not found error. If the seller has been deleted or is otherwise unavailable, the response should follow the platform’s standard access and lifecycle error handling.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the seller account by its UUID primary key from mall_platform_seller_accounts and join the optional mall_platform_seller_profiles relation to include public shop data. Return the current account fields including email, approval status, rejection reason, suspended_at, deleted_at, created_at, and updated_at, plus the linked seller profile when present.

Do not expose password_hash. Preserve the current lifecycle state exactly as stored; do not infer approval from related tables. If the record does not exist, return 404. If the caller is not permitted to view the seller, return the platform’s standard authorization error. When the related profile is missing, return the seller record with a null or absent profile component according to the response schema.

responseBody.description: The seller account details together with its linked public shop profile, if available.

parameters.description: Seller account identifier (UUID primary key).
parameters.name: sellerId

operations.description:
Search and browse administrator accounts for platform governance.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of administrator summaries so authorized administrative users can review administrator accounts, privilege grade, and account status from a single collection view. It is intended for governance and oversight workflows rather than self-service account management.

Filtering, sorting, and pagination are provided through the request body so the client can drive review screens efficiently. The service must enforce administrator-level authorization before querying, apply deterministic ordering, and reject invalid pagination or filter values with a validation error. Sensitive credential data must not be exposed in the response.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the mall_platform_administrators table for administrative browsing.
Apply request-body filters for account status, privilege grade, and keyword search if the shared DTO contract defines them.
Support pagination and sorting from the request body, defaulting to a deterministic order when the client omits sort settings.
Return summary rows only; do not include password hashes or other authentication secrets.
Enforce authorization so only administrators can access the collection.
If no rows match, return an empty page with valid pagination metadata. If filters or pagination values are invalid, return a validation error rather than a partial result.

responseBody.description: Paginated administrator summary records suitable for governance screens.

requestBody.description: Pagination, search, and sorting criteria for browsing administrator accounts.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single administrator account by its UUID identifier.

This operation supports platform governance and administrative account inspection. It returns the administrator's identity, grade, status, and lifecycle timestamps as stored in the administrator table.

The response does not include the password hash or any session-related data. If the administrator record does not exist, the request fails with a not-found error. If the caller is not authorized to inspect administrator accounts, the request fails with an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch the administrator row from mall_platform_administrators by primary key id.
Project the record into the public administrator DTO and exclude password_hash from the response.
Do not join session or password reset tables because this endpoint is limited to the account record itself.
Use the path parameter as a UUID lookup key and return 404 when no record matches.
Preserve the stored deleted_at value only if the public administrator DTO is designed to expose lifecycle metadata; otherwise omit it from the API response and keep it internal.
Surface authorization failures through the standard access control layer before any database read is returned.

responseBody.description: The administrator account identified by the requested UUID.

parameters.description: The administrator account identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: administratorId

operations.description:
Lists administrator approval requests for governance review and oversight.

This endpoint returns a paginated set of administrator approval requests so super administrators can review pending submissions and inspect historical decisions. The data reflects the request lifecycle stored in the administrator approval request table, including the applicant, review status, rejection details, and timestamps.

Filtering and sorting should follow the platform’s administrative browsing expectations. Typical filters include status, reason keywords, and reviewer identity, with sorting by creation time or review time depending on the client’s needs. Because this is an administrative oversight view, access must be restricted to authorized super administrators.

If a request does not exist or is not visible to the caller due to authorization rules, the service should respond with the appropriate access or not-found error according to the platform’s standard error handling.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests with pagination, search, and sort controls from the request body. Support filtering by status, reviewer administrator, reason keyword, and date ranges if those fields are provided by the request DTO. Order results by the requested sort key, defaulting to newest first by created_at.

Return a paginated summary projection rather than full records. The summary should include the request identity, applicant administrator reference, reason, status, rejection_reason, reviewed_at, created_at, updated_at, and reviewer administrator reference when present. Exclude deleted rows from the result set.

Enforce super-administrator authorization before querying. If the caller lacks permission, return a forbidden error. If the client requests a request that is inaccessible according to governance rules, return not found or forbidden consistently with the platform standard. Ensure pagination is stable and deterministic.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of administrator approval request summaries for governance review.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for administrator approval requests, including status filtering, text search, sorting, and page controls.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single administrator approval request for governance review.

This endpoint returns the full administrator approval request identified by the requestId path parameter so a super administrator can inspect the applicant’s reason, review status, and final decision details.

The operation is read-only and supports platform governance only. If the request does not exist, the service should return a not-found error. If the caller lacks super administrator privileges, the service should return an authorization error. The response reflects the current persisted record for the approval request.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests by requestId and return the full administrator approval request record.
Include the applicant reference, submitted reason, current status, reviewer decision metadata, and lifecycle timestamps as defined by the entity contract.
Do not modify the request, create snapshots, or trigger approval workflow side effects.
Enforce super administrator authorization before reading the record. If no row matches requestId, return not found. If the caller is not permitted, return forbidden.

responseBody.description: The full administrator approval request record for governance review.

parameters.description: The administrator approval request identifier (UUID).
parameters.name: requestId

operations.description:
Returns the signed-in customer’s current profile information.

This endpoint exposes the customer-facing identity details associated with the authenticated customer account. The returned profile contains the current display name and phone number used for presentation and contact across the platform.

Access is limited to authenticated customers. Because the profile is resolved from the current session, no path parameter or request body is required. If the caller is not signed in, the request should be rejected as unauthorized. If the customer profile cannot be resolved for the authenticated account, the request should fail with a not-found style error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated customer from the current session, then load the associated mall_platform_customer_profiles record for that customer account. Return the full current customer profile for the authenticated account only.

Do not accept any identifier in the path or request body. Do not expose other customers’ profile data. If the session does not belong to an authenticated customer, return an authorization error. If no profile record exists for the account, return an appropriate not-found error. This operation must remain read-only and must not create or modify any profile data.

responseBody.description: The authenticated customer’s profile record containing the current display name and phone number.

operations.description:
List the authenticated customer's saved shipping addresses.

This endpoint returns the address book owned by the current customer account so the UI can display saved delivery destinations for checkout and profile management. It supports pagination and browsing behavior for customers who maintain multiple addresses.

Only the authenticated customer's own addresses are returned. The response should include the data needed for the address list view, including the default address indicator if available in the underlying schema. If no addresses exist, the endpoint returns an empty page rather than an error.

Validation errors should be reported when search or pagination criteria are invalid. Unauthorized requests must be rejected.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_shipping_addresses for the authenticated customer only.

Apply filter, sort, and pagination criteria from the request body. Return a paginated result set with a total count and summary rows suitable for address list screens. The implementation must never expose another customer's addresses.

If the schema includes address identity, recipient, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, country, and default-selection fields, map them into the summary DTO. Do not include order-specific shipping data here; this is strictly the saved address book.

Reject invalid request-body input with a 400-level error. Reject unauthenticated access with an authorization error. Return an empty page when the customer has no saved addresses.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the authenticated customer's saved shipping address summaries.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for the authenticated customer's saved shipping addresses.

operations.description:
Create a new shipping address for the authenticated customer.

Customers can keep multiple saved shipping addresses, and each address belongs to exactly one customer account. The newly created address becomes available for checkout and future deliveries immediately after it is saved.

A shipping address must include the recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, and country. If any required delivery detail is missing or invalid, the request must be rejected and no partial address record should be created. Failed creation does not affect the customer’s existing saved addresses.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new shipping address row for the currently authenticated customer account.

Use the authentication context to determine ownership; do not accept a customer identifier in the request body. Validate that the request contains all required shipping address fields before insert: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, and country. Reject incomplete or invalid payloads and perform the create atomically so there is no partial persistence.

After insertion, return the created shipping address exactly as persisted. Do not modify other addresses as part of this operation. Do not attempt to apply default-address behavior unless the schema and create DTO explicitly support it.

responseBody.description: The shipping address that was successfully created for the authenticated customer.

requestBody.description: The shipping address details to save, including the delivery contact and location information required for checkout and shipment delivery.

operations.description:
Retrieve a saved shipping address by its identifier.

This operation returns the full shipping address record stored under a customer account. The address contains the recipient, contact, and location fields used for delivery, along with the default-address flag used in checkout selection.

The caller can only access addresses that belong to their own customer account. If the address does not exist, is deleted, or belongs to another customer, the request must fail with a not-found response. No data is modified by this operation.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch one row from mall_platform_shipping_addresses by id.
Enforce authenticated customer ownership so the caller can only read their own shipping address. Exclude deleted rows from lookup. Return the complete entity fields available in the schema: id, customer_id, recipient_name, phone_number, street_address, city, state_province, postal_code, country, is_default, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

Do not infer or require any extra fields beyond the schema. If no matching row is found, return a not-found error. This endpoint is read-only and must not mutate the address record.

responseBody.description: The complete saved shipping address record for the requested customer-owned destination.

parameters.description: The shipping address UUID to retrieve (customer-scoped).
parameters.name: shippingAddressId

operations.description:
Update an existing shipping address for the current customer.

This operation replaces the editable delivery details of a saved shipping address, including recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, and country. A successfully updated address remains available for future checkout use.

The address must belong to the authenticated customer, and it cannot be changed once it has been used for a placed order. If validation fails or the update cannot be completed, the previously saved address values remain unchanged and no partial update is applied.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Fetch the shipping address by its ID and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer. Reject requests that target another customer’s address.

Before applying changes, confirm that the address is not locked by order history. If the address is already part of a placed order and the business rule marks it immutable, return a conflict-style error and do not modify the record.

Apply updates only to the mutable shipping address fields defined in the schema: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, and country. Do not alter ownership or any other system-managed fields unless they are explicitly part of the schema and business rules.

Perform the update within a transaction so that any validation error leaves the record exactly as it was before the request. Return the updated full shipping address entity after a successful save.

responseBody.description: The updated shipping address after the changes have been saved successfully.

parameters.description: The shipping address identifier to update.
parameters.name: shippingAddressId

requestBody.description: The editable shipping address fields used to replace the existing address details.

operations.description:
Delete one saved shipping address owned by the current customer.

This operation removes a customer-owned shipping address from the saved list so it can no longer be selected during checkout. If the address is currently marked as the default shipping address, the system clears that default designation before completing the deletion so the customer does not keep a default address pointing to a removed record.

Only the owning customer may delete the address. If the address does not exist, was already removed, or belongs to another customer, the system must not alter any remaining saved addresses. A failed or repeated delete request must leave the customer’s saved address list unchanged.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Look up the shipping address by shippingAddressId and ensure it belongs to the authenticated customer account. If the address is present and owned by the caller, perform the deletion in a single transaction. When the target address is currently marked as the default shipping address, clear the default flag before deleting the row so no deleted address remains selected as default. If the address is missing, already deleted, or not owned by the caller, return the appropriate not-found or forbidden error according to platform authorization rules and do not modify any remaining addresses. The operation must be idempotent from the customer perspective and must not partially update other shipping address records.

parameters.description: The shipping address identifier within the customer's saved address list.
parameters.name: shippingAddressId

operations.description:
Mark a saved shipping address as the customer's default address.

This operation changes the selected shipping address so it becomes the preferred delivery destination for future checkout flows. The address must belong to the authenticated customer, and only one saved address may be default at a time.

If the address is owned by another customer or cannot be updated, the request must be rejected and no changes may be applied. When a new default is selected, any previous default address for the same customer must be cleared in the same transaction so the customer never has more than one default address.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Resolve the shipping address by shippingAddressId and verify that it belongs to the authenticated customer. Reject the request with a not-found or forbidden response if the record is missing or not owned by the caller.

Execute the change in a transaction. Clear the default designation from any other shipping address owned by the same customer, then set the target address as the default. Preserve all other address fields unchanged. If the target is already the default, return it as-is without changing other rows.

If any validation or persistence step fails, roll back the transaction so the customer's saved address list remains unchanged. Return the updated shipping address entity on success.

responseBody.description: The shipping address after it has been marked as the customer's default address.

parameters.description: The identifier of the shipping address to mark as default.
parameters.name: shippingAddressId

operations.description:
Search and list seller accounts with pagination and sorting.

This endpoint returns a paginated collection of seller account summary records for browsing and moderation workflows. It is intended for administrative review screens and other account-management interfaces that need to inspect seller account state, approval status, and related identity information at scale.

Filtering and sorting should follow the platform browsing rules for list views. The implementation must respect account availability constraints, exclude records that are not meant to appear in the current browsing context, and return stable paginated results. Validation failures should be reported when the request contains unsupported filter values or pagination parameters.

Because this is a collection endpoint, it does not return a single seller account detail object. Consumers should use the corresponding detail endpoint for a single seller account when needed.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the mall_platform_sellers and mall_platform_seller_accounts data needed to build a searchable seller account list. Apply pagination, keyword search, approval-status filtering, and sorting in the service layer before returning results.

Use seller account and approval-related fields that are actually available in the schema. Do not invent status columns or lifecycle timestamps. If the request includes a search keyword, match against seller identity fields and any public account identifiers supported by the schema. If the request includes approval state criteria, filter by the seller approval relationship rather than assuming a denormalized field exists on the seller table.

Return summary rows only, not full account entities, and include enough data for list displays such as account identity and approval state information. Ensure pagination metadata is correct and deterministic. If the requested page is out of range, return an empty page rather than failing unless the platform's global validation rules require an error.

Reject unsupported sort keys and filter values with a validation error. Preserve authorization boundaries so only permitted actors can access seller account browsing data.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of seller account summary records matching the search criteria.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering, sorting, and paginating seller account records.

operations.description:
Retrieve a seller account and its linked shop profile.

This operation returns the current seller account record, including the email login identity, approval status, rejection reason, suspension state, deletion state, and lifecycle timestamps. It also returns the seller profile associated with the account so consumers can display the shop name, shop description, and logo image together with the account state.

The seller account is identified by its UUID primary key. If the account does not exist, the service must return a not-found error. The response must reflect the stored lifecycle state exactly as recorded, and it must never expose the password hash.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load one mall_platform_seller_accounts record by primary key and join the one-to-one mall_platform_seller_profiles relation through seller_account_id. Return the seller account fields id, email, approval_status, rejection_reason, suspended_at, deleted_at, created_at, and updated_at, plus the linked seller profile fields id, seller_account_id, shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_uri, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

Validate sellerAccountId as a UUID before querying. If the seller account is missing, return a 404-style error. Do not expose password_hash in any response mapping. Do not infer approval or suspension from the profile table; the seller account table is authoritative for account state. Keep nullable columns nullable in the response and preserve exact stored values.

responseBody.description: A seller account detail record including the linked seller profile.

parameters.description: The seller account UUID to retrieve (global scope).
parameters.name: sellerAccountId

operations.description:
Returns the authenticated seller’s account record, including its current approval state and any rejection reason.

This endpoint is used by seller-facing pages that need to display the account’s registration status without exposing other sellers’ data. The seller account status is represented as pending, approved, or rejected, and if the account has been rejected the response includes the rejection reason so the seller can understand the review outcome.

The operation reads the seller account in the current authentication context and does not require a path parameter. If the caller is not authenticated as a seller or the account is otherwise inaccessible, the request should fail with an authorization or access error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Load the authenticated seller account from the seller session context. Query the mall_platform_seller_accounts table for the current seller identity and join any related fields needed for the response schema, including approval status and rejection reason if present. Do not accept a seller ID parameter because the route is scoped to the currently signed-in seller. Return a not-found or forbidden-style error if the session is missing, invalid, or not a seller session. Preserve the read-only nature of the operation and avoid exposing fields outside the seller account contract.

responseBody.description: The authenticated seller account with its current approval state and rejection reason when applicable.

operations.description:
Retrieve a seller profile for storefront and profile display.

This operation returns the current seller profile identified by `sellerProfileId`, including the public shop identity used across product listings, seller profile pages, and order-history references. Customers can use it to understand who is selling a product, and the owning seller can use it to view the current state of their public profile.

The response reflects current seller profile data only. Seller profile edits are preserved separately through snapshots, and this endpoint does not create, update, or expose historical versions. If the seller profile cannot be found, the server should return a not-found response. Access should follow platform permissions so authenticated customers can view public seller profiles, while the owning seller and administrators can access the same resource according to their normal visibility rules.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the seller profile by its primary identifier and return the current profile row only. Validate that the record exists; otherwise return 404.

Use the seller profile table as the source of truth for current storefront identity fields. Do not join or modify snapshot tables in this operation. The endpoint must remain read-only and must not trigger snapshot creation.

Include the fields required for storefront presentation, specifically shop name, shop description, and logo image reference. If account-state restrictions make the profile unavailable under business rules, handle it as not found or forbidden according to the platform's access policy.

responseBody.description: The current seller profile record used for customer-facing storefront and seller-facing profile views.

parameters.description: The seller profile identifier (UUID).
parameters.name: sellerProfileId

Retrieve a seller profile for storefront and profile display.

This operation returns the current seller profile identified by `sellerProfileId`, including the public shop identity used across product listings, seller profile pages, and order-history references. Customers can use it to understand who is selling a product, and the owning seller can use it to view the current state of their public profile.

operations.name: at

Load the seller profile by its primary identifier and return the current profile row only. Validate that the record exists; otherwise return 404.

Use the seller profile table as the source of truth for current storefront identity fields. Do not join or modify snapshot tables in this operation. The endpoint must remain read-only and must not trigger snapshot creation.

Include the fields required for storefront presentation, specifically shop name, shop description, and logo image reference. If account-state restrictions make the profile unavailable under business rules, handle it as not found or forbidden according to the platform's access policy.
