operations.description:
Search and list shipments with pagination, filtering, and sorting.

Shipments represent seller-specific delivery packages that may contain one or more order items from the same seller and share one set of tracking details. This endpoint is intended for order history screens, seller fulfillment views, and administrative browsing of shipment records.

Customers should only see shipments that belong to their own orders, sellers should only see shipments that contain their own order items, and administrators may browse all shipments. If the search matches no records, the response should be an empty page rather than an error.

Validation errors should be returned for unsupported filters, invalid pagination values, or malformed sorting rules. This endpoint does not modify shipment data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query mall_platform_shipments as the primary table and join mall_platform_shipment_items plus mall_platform_order_items when filtering by order scope, seller scope, or item membership. Apply pagination, keyword search, and sorting from the request body, then return shipment summary rows only.

Enforce actor-based visibility in the query layer: customers may only read shipments related to their own orders, sellers may only read shipments containing their own items, and administrators may read all shipments. Reject unsupported criteria, invalid page values, and impossible sort requests with validation errors rather than silently ignoring them.

Do not mutate any shipment rows in this operation. Completed shipments remain readable as historical records, but duplicate shipment creation or resubmission is outside the scope of this list endpoint.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of shipment summary records matching the search criteria.

requestBody.description: Shipment search criteria including pagination, sorting, and shipment-related filters.

operations.description:
Create a shipment for one seller's eligible order items.

This operation creates a new shipment package with shared tracking information and links the selected order items to it. It is used in the seller fulfillment workflow so customers can later view which items travel together inside the same shipment from their order history.

Every item in the shipment must belong to the same seller and must still be waiting to ship. If any selected item is already shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, or assigned to another shipment, the request must fail and no shipment should be created. When creation succeeds, the included order items are updated to shipped status in the same transaction.

The response should include the created shipment and its linked items so the caller can immediately show tracking details. Validation errors should clearly identify missing tracking information, empty item selection, mixed-seller item selection, and duplicate or ineligible items.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Treat this as a transactional shipment-creation workflow.

Load the requested order items and verify that every item belongs to the authenticated seller. Reject the request if any item is not owned by that seller, if the items come from different sellers, or if any item is not in a shippable state.

Enforce the one-shipment-per-eligible-item rule. Before inserting anything, confirm that none of the selected items already belongs to an active shipment and that the same item is not duplicated in the request.

Create the shipment row and its shipment-item linkage rows in a single transaction. Persist the carrier name and tracking number from the request, then update all included order items to shipped status after the shipment is created.

Return the created shipment with its tracking fields and included order items. If validation fails, roll back the full transaction and return a domain error rather than creating a partial shipment.

responseBody.description: The shipment that was created, including its tracking information and included order items.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation details including the seller's eligible order items and the shipment tracking information.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single shipment with its tracking details and included order items.

This endpoint returns the shipment header for one package created by a seller, including carrier information, tracking number, shipment status, shipped and delivered timestamps, and the order items assigned to that shipment. It is used in order history and shipment detail views so customers can see how their items are grouped for delivery.

The shipment is identified by its UUID path parameter. The response should reflect the current shipment record together with its related shipment items so the consumer can display which order items travel together. If the shipment does not exist, return a not-found error. If the shipment belongs to an order the caller is not allowed to view, return an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by primary key and include its shipmentItems relation, with each linked orderItem and the minimal nested order-item references needed for display. Use a single transaction-free read query because this is a pure retrieval operation.

Validate that shipmentId is a UUID and return 404 when no shipment exists for the given id. Do not infer or compute shipment membership from orders; use the persisted shipment-item junction records. The response must expose current carrier_name, tracking_number, tracking_url, status, shipped_at, delivered_at, created_at, and updated_at values from mall_platform_shipments.

Preserve access control according to actor rules: customers may read shipments that belong to their own orders, sellers may read shipments for their own seller-owned orders/items, and administrators may read any shipment. If authorization fails, return 403. If the shipment has been deleted or is otherwise unavailable in persistence, treat it as not found.

responseBody.description: The full shipment record with related shipment items for display in order history and shipment detail views.

parameters.description: The shipment UUID identifier (global scope).
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Update a shipment's carrier, tracking information, or status.

This endpoint updates the shipment header for an existing seller shipment tied to a single order. It is used to correct carrier details, record tracking information, and advance shipment status as fulfillment progresses. Shipment membership is preserved, so the included order items are not reassigned by this operation.

The service must verify that the shipment exists, is not deleted, and is accessible to the caller according to seller ownership or administrator privileges. A completed shipment must not be reopened or resubmitted, and invalid lifecycle transitions must be rejected without partially updating the record. If the request changes the status to shipped or delivered, the corresponding timestamp fields should be populated when they are still empty.

If the shipment is not found, return a not-found error. If the caller lacks permission to modify it, return an authorization or ownership error. If the requested update conflicts with shipment lifecycle rules or tracking-number uniqueness within the seller scope, return a validation error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by id together with its seller, order, and shipmentItems relations. Verify that the caller is the owning seller or an administrator with shipment management privileges. Reject missing or deleted shipments.

Update only the shipment header fields exposed by the request body: carrier name, tracking number, tracking URL, and status. Never modify shipment item membership in this endpoint. Enforce the unique constraint on tracking_number combined with mall_platform_seller_id before persisting changes.

Disallow status changes that would reopen a shipment already marked delivered or otherwise completed. When transitioning to shipped, set shipped_at if it is null. When transitioning to delivered, set delivered_at if it is null. Keep the transaction atomic so the shipment record cannot be partially updated. Return the refreshed shipment after commit.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment record including carrier, tracking, status, and fulfillment timestamps.

parameters.description: The shipment identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: The shipment fields that can be updated, including carrier information, tracking details, and status.

operations.description:
Delete a shipment record.

This endpoint removes a seller-specific shipment package identified by its UUID. It is intended for shipment lifecycle cleanup when a shipment must no longer be available in the active fulfillment flow.

The shipment belongs to one seller and one order, and it may have one or more shipment item assignments through the shipment-items relation. Implementations must verify the shipment exists before deletion and enforce business rules so that active fulfillment history is not corrupted. Because shipment items are linked by cascade relations, deleting the shipment should also remove its shipment-item assignments through the database relationship handling.

If the shipment does not exist, return a not-found error. If the shipment is already finalized or otherwise cannot be removed by policy, return a conflict or forbidden-style error according to the service error conventions.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Load the shipment by id and confirm it exists. Enforce authorization so only permitted seller/admin actors can delete it according to platform rules. Before deletion, consider the shipment status and prevent removal if the shipment is already delivered or otherwise locked by downstream business policy. Delete the shipment row and allow the database cascade to remove linked shipment-item rows. Do not modify order item records directly in this operation. Return a not-found error when the shipment id is invalid or missing, and map business rule violations to conflict/forbidden errors.

parameters.description: The shipment UUID to delete.
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Updates the order items assigned to a shipment.

This endpoint supports seller fulfillment by reconciling the membership of an existing shipment package. A shipment is the delivery unit for one seller, and every order item in that shipment must belong to the same seller and the same order. The server must validate those ownership and eligibility rules before applying any change.

The request is treated as the desired final set of order items for the shipment. The service should add missing shipment-item rows and remove rows that are no longer included, all inside one transaction. It must reject items that already belong to another shipment, items that belong to a different seller, items from a different order, or items that are not in a shippable state. If the resulting shipment would be empty, the request should be rejected.

Shipment header data such as carrier name, tracking number, tracking URL, shipped time, delivered time, and status must not be modified by this operation. Only the shipment-item junction table should change, and the update should fail atomically if any requested item is invalid.
operations.name: patchByShipmentid
operations.specification:
Load the shipment by id and verify that it exists and is not deleted. Use the shipment's seller id and order id as the validation scope.

Interpret the request body as the desired final set of order item identifiers for the shipment. Compare the requested set with the current mall_platform_shipment_items rows for that shipment. Insert missing rows and remove rows not present in the request within a single transaction.

For every requested order item, confirm that mall_platform_order_items.mall_platform_order_id matches the shipment's order, mall_platform_order_items.mall_platform_seller_id matches the shipment's seller, and the item is eligible for shipment. Also confirm that the item is not already assigned to another shipment-item row, since mall_platform_shipment_items enforces uniqueness on mall_platform_order_item_id. If any item fails validation, reject the entire request.

Do not update shipment carrier or status fields here. Do not allow cross-seller or cross-order composition. Reject requests that would leave the shipment with zero items if business rules require shipments to contain at least one order item. Return the updated shipment entity after commit.

responseBody.description: The shipment after its item membership has been updated.

parameters.description: The shipment identifier (UUID) whose item membership is being updated.
parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: The desired final set of order item identifiers to include in the shipment.

operations.description:
Creates shipment item links for an existing shipment and attaches eligible order items to that delivery package.

A shipment is the platform's delivery unit and must contain only order items from the same seller. This operation is used during seller fulfillment to bundle one or more shippable order items into a single shipment. The system must reject any request that mixes sellers, includes an order item that is already assigned to another shipment, or includes an item that is no longer eligible for shipping.

The created shipment-item records support order detail tracking and customer delivery confirmation. If any requested item fails validation, the entire request must be rejected without creating a partial shipment assignment.

operations.description:
Updates a shipment item assignment within a shipment.

This endpoint manages the junction record that associates one order item with one shipment. It is used to revise shipment membership while preserving the shipment header data such as carrier and tracking information.

The service must ensure that the specified shipment item belongs to the shipment identified by the path, that the related order item still belongs to the same seller as the shipment, and that the order item is not already assigned to another shipment. Any change that would violate shipment grouping rules, duplicate the order item assignment, or modify shipment header data must be rejected.

If the shipment item does not exist, the service returns a not found error. If the requested update would break delivery grouping constraints or item uniqueness, the service returns a validation or conflict error. Successful updates must be transactional and must refresh the record timestamps.

Join the shipment and order item records to confirm the shipment and item share the same seller context and that the item remains eligible for assignment. Enforce the unique constraint on mall_platform_order_item_id so one order item cannot be linked to multiple shipments. If the update would move the item to a different shipment, verify the target shipment is also valid for that seller and has not violated any shipment state restrictions.

Use a transaction for the update to avoid race conditions with concurrent fulfillment actions. Do not update shipment carrier/tracking/status fields in this operation because those live on mall_platform_shipments, not on the junction table. If the platform forbids editing shipment membership after shipping or delivery, return a validation failure. Return the updated shipment-item record after persistence.

operations.description:
Remove one order item from a shipment.

This operation deletes the shipment-item association while leaving the shipment and the underlying order item intact. It is used to correct a shipment before fulfillment is finalized, such as when items need to be repacked or moved into a different seller-specific shipment.

The item must belong to the specified shipment, and the caller must be authorized to manage that shipment. If the shipment or shipment item does not exist, if the item belongs to another shipment, or if the shipment is locked by its lifecycle state, the request must fail with the appropriate not-found, forbidden, or conflict error.

Delete only the association row from mall_platform_shipment_items. Do not delete the shipment record, the order item record, or any order history. Before deletion, check shipment state rules to ensure the shipment is still editable. Also ensure the deletion will not violate shipment integrity expectations; if the shipment must not become empty according to current business rules or implementation constraints, reject with a conflict.

Return a consistent error for missing shipment, missing shipment item, cross-shipment mismatch, unauthorized access, and locked shipment state. If the implementation returns a response body, it should be the refreshed shipment aggregate with remaining items and tracking information; otherwise return no content.

operations.description:
Submit a cancellation request for one paid, unshipped order item.

This endpoint lets a customer request cancellation for a specific purchased item instead of the entire order. The request is tied to one order item and carries the customer's reason for review by the item's seller.

The request is accepted only when the target order item belongs to the authenticated customer, is still in paid status, and has not been shipped. If the item is unavailable for cancellation, the system rejects the request without changing the order item, sibling items, inventory, or any existing cancellation history.

Load the target order item by orderItemId and verify ownership against the authenticated customer. Reject the request if the order item does not exist, is not owned by the caller, is already shipped, or is in any terminal state that makes cancellation invalid.

Check whether the domain allows only one active cancellation request per order item. If a request already exists and duplicate requests are not permitted, reject the operation without creating another record.

On success, create a new cancellation request row bound to exactly one order item and persist the customer-provided reason and initial pending review state. Do not update the order item status, inventory, shipments, or any sibling order items here; those effects occur only after seller review. Return the created cancellation request entity.

Persist any request snapshot/audit data required by the domain model when the request is later reviewed. Do not modify order item status, inventory, refund state, or shipment data at creation time. Keep the operation atomic so a failed validation leaves the order item unchanged.

If either record is missing, or if the request does not belong to the specified item, the operation should return a normal business error response.

This is a read-only endpoint and must not modify cancellation state, create snapshots, restore inventory, or alter order-item status. Those effects belong to the cancellation review workflow on the write side.

operations.description:
Resolve a cancellation request for one order item.

This operation allows the seller responsible for the specified order item to approve or reject a cancellation request that was submitted for that exact item. The request is scoped to both the order item and cancellation request identifiers in the path, so the server must confirm the request belongs to the item before applying any change.

A cancellation request is only valid while the order item remains in paid status and has not been shipped. If the seller approves the request, the item is cancelled, a refund is triggered for that item only, stock is restored through an inventory record, and the previous request state is preserved in a snapshot. If the seller rejects the request, the order item remains unchanged and the request is closed with the recorded rejection outcome.

Only the owning seller or an authorized administrator may perform this action. If the order item, request, or account state is unavailable, or if the item no longer qualifies for cancellation, the server must reject the request without changing unrelated items or records.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the order item and cancellation request by their identifiers, then verify that the cancellation request belongs to the specified order item. Reject the operation if either record is missing, the request is already resolved, the order item is not in paid status, or the item has been shipped.

Validate the incoming update payload for the seller decision and any optional note fields. Execute the decision inside a single transaction. On approval, update the cancellation request state, create a cancellation-request snapshot, mark the order item as cancelled, create the inventory record that restores stock, and invoke any refund side effects required by the platform flow. On rejection, update the request state and create the snapshot without changing the order item.

The operation must be atomic. If snapshot creation, order-item status change, inventory restoration, or refund processing fails, roll back the transaction so no partial update is persisted. Return the updated cancellation request after successful completion.

Because snapshots are immutable historical records, no update or delete behavior should be implemented here.

operations.description:
Lists or searches refund requests for a specific order item.

This endpoint returns the live refund request record associated with the given order item, if one exists, and supports paginated browsing when the response is treated as a collection search. It is intended for the customer who submitted the request, the responsible seller, and administrators who need to inspect the current refund workflow in the context of a purchased item.

Refund requests are scoped to a single order item and the database enforces that only one request can exist per item. The service must validate the order item first, then query refund requests by mall_platform_order_item_id. Historical changes are preserved separately in refund request snapshot records and must not be altered by this operation.

If the order item does not exist, or the caller is not allowed to view the request for that item, the request must fail with the appropriate business error. If no refund request exists yet, return an empty page rather than inventing a record.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Validate that the target order item exists and load it as the scope boundary. Query mall_platform_refund_requests by mall_platform_order_item_id and apply pagination, filtering, and sorting from the request body.

Use the unique constraint on mall_platform_refund_requests.mall_platform_order_item_id to preserve the one-request-per-item rule. This endpoint must remain read-only and must not create, update, or delete refund requests or snapshots.

If the caller is the owning customer, the item's seller, or an administrator, return the current refund request data. If the order item is missing, return not found. If the caller lacks permission, return forbidden. Do not join snapshot history into the live list response; snapshots are separate immutable records for dispute review.

operations.description:
Create a refund request for a delivered order item.

This endpoint lets a customer submit an item-level refund request for a specific order item, not for the entire order. The request records the customer’s reason and starts the review flow for that item only, while all other items in the order remain unchanged.

The order item must be eligible for refund according to the business rules: it must already be delivered, must not already have an active refund request, and must not be in a conflicting terminal state such as cancelled or already refunded. If the item is not eligible, the system rejects the request as a normal business error and does not create a refund request.

When creation succeeds, the refund request is stored under the specified order item and its later status changes are preserved through snapshots for dispute review and historical reconstruction.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target order item by orderItemId and verify that it exists. Enforce the refund eligibility rules before insertion: the item must be delivered, must not already be refunded, must not be cancelled, and must not have an existing active refund request. If any condition fails, return a business error without changing the order item or creating a partial record.

Create the refund request as an item-scoped subsidiary record linked to the order item. The request body should only supply the customer-provided reason and any other create-time fields defined by the refund request schema; do not accept the path identifier in the payload. Perform the duplicate-active-request check and insert atomically in one transaction to avoid race conditions. After creation, return the persisted refund request entity. Any later seller review action must create immutable snapshots of the request state.

The operation is read-only and intended for authorized customers, sellers, and administrators who need to inspect refund status and review history. If the order item does not exist, the refund request does not belong to that item, or the record is unavailable, the service must return a business not-found error without exposing unrelated records.

operations.description:
Updates a refund request for a specific order item.

This operation changes the current state of a refund request that belongs to one order item. Refund handling is item-level, so the update must remain scoped to the specified order item and cannot affect other items in the order. When the request changes, the system must preserve the prior state in an immutable snapshot for dispute review and history reconstruction.

The request is only valid while the order item remains eligible for refund handling. If the refund request does not belong to the given order item, if the item is no longer eligible, or if the requested change conflicts with another active refund workflow, the system must reject the operation without modifying unrelated records.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Fetch the refund request by refundRequestId and verify that its orderItemId matches the path parameter. Reject the request if the association does not match or if the target request is missing.

Before applying the update, confirm that the order item is still eligible for refund processing based on the business rules: the item must be delivered, the request must not be a duplicate active refund request, and the requested state transition must be allowed. If the update changes the review state or other mutable fields, create an immutable snapshot of the previous request state in the same transaction before saving the new state.

Apply the update atomically so no partial change is visible. Do not modify unrelated order items, orders, inventory history, or other refund requests. Return a business error or not-found response when the target request is missing, mismatched, or ineligible.

Snapshots are append-only historical records and must never be modified or deleted through this API. If the order item does not exist, the refund request does not exist, or the refund request is not associated with the specified order item, the request must fail with a not-found response. Use pagination and stable sorting so clients can safely browse long histories.

operations.description:
Lists the active public reviews for a product, ordered by newest first.

This endpoint scopes review browsing to a single product and returns the review feed that appears on the product detail page. Reviews are purchase-based feedback from customers, so the data is intended for public reputation display rather than private account management.

The response is paginated because a product may accumulate many reviews. Deleted reviews must be excluded from the active listing and from any visible count used by the product detail page. The service should preserve the newest-first browsing rule so the latest feedback appears first.

Apply pagination and any supported list filters from the request body according to the platform browsing rules. If customer display data is needed for the summary DTO, join the owning customer only for public-safe fields. Return a paginated summary response suitable for the product detail page. If the product does not exist, return the standard not-found error. Do not expose deleted review rows in this endpoint.

operations.description:
Create a new review for a delivered purchase item.

A customer may submit a review only after the related order item has been delivered, and only once per product within the same order. The review becomes visible on the product detail page and contributes to the product’s review count and average rating while it remains active.

The service must verify that the authenticated customer owns the purchase context, that the referenced order item is eligible for review, and that no other review already exists for the same product within the same order. If any eligibility check fails, the request must be rejected without creating a review.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Use the authenticated customer session to resolve ownership and enforce review eligibility. Validate that the request references a delivered order item belonging to the current customer, and confirm that no active review already exists for the same product within the same order.

Create the review in mall_platform_reviews and, if the implementation persists historical state at creation time, also create the corresponding snapshot record in mall_platform_review_snapshots in the same transaction. Do not accept system-managed fields from the client; derive identity, ownership, and timestamps server-side.

Return a conflict error for duplicate reviews, a forbidden or validation error for unauthorized or ineligible purchases, and a not-found error when the purchase context cannot be resolved. Preserve deleted-user review visibility by keeping review identity separate from customer account deletion behavior.

responseBody.description: The newly created review persisted by the system.

requestBody.description: Review content and purchase context for a delivered order item, including the rating, optional text, and references needed to verify that the caller is allowed to review the product.

operations.description:
Return a single review with its linked purchase and product context.

This endpoint retrieves one review by identifier so clients can display the review detail, including the star rating and optional written content. The review is tied to a specific customer, order item, and product, which supports product detail pages, ownership validation, and dispute review.

Only the review owner and administrators should be able to access this resource when privacy rules apply. If the review has been deleted, the historical record may still exist in storage, but clients must respect its active state and display rules. A missing identifier should produce a not-found response.

Enforce access control so the owning customer can read their own review and administrators can read any review. Preserve deleted review records as historical data, but do not expose snapshot history here; snapshots are handled by the review snapshot subsystem. Return not found when the review id does not exist or is not accessible.

operations.description:
Updates an existing customer review.

This endpoint lets the original author change the star rating and optional written comment for a previously submitted review. The review remains linked to the purchase context, and the prior state must be preserved in a snapshot before the active record is updated.

Only the customer who created the review may update it. If the review does not exist, belongs to another customer, or fails validation, the request must be rejected with the appropriate error response. Because reviews appear on product detail pages and contribute to rating summaries, the updated review should be returned so clients can refresh the displayed content immediately.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Look up the active review by reviewId and ensure it exists. Verify the authenticated customer is the review owner before allowing the edit; unauthorized attempts must be rejected without exposing another user's review data.

Validate the request body fields. The rating must satisfy the review rating constraints, and the text content, if present, should be persisted as the review body. Do not allow changes to immutable context fields such as the customer, product, or order-item linkage.

Before saving the new values, create an immutable review snapshot containing the previous state so edit history is preserved. Then update the active review record and return the updated entity. Return not found when the review does not exist and validation errors when the payload is invalid.

operations.description:
Delete a review while preserving its historical snapshot trail.

This endpoint removes the active review record for a single review identified by reviewId. The system must verify that the current customer owns the review before allowing deletion. If the review has already been deleted or the caller is not allowed to delete it, the request must fail with the appropriate authorization or not-found error.

Review deletion must preserve historical data. The previous review state remains available through snapshot records, and deleted reviews must no longer contribute to active review listings or product average rating calculations. Preserved review history must continue to display as written by a deleted user when the original customer account no longer exists.

Before removing the active review, create a review snapshot that preserves the current review state for history and dispute review. Keep the snapshot immutable.
Delete or deactivate the active review row so it no longer appears in normal product detail review listings and no longer affects average rating calculations.
If the review is already removed or inaccessible, return a not-found style error. If ownership validation fails, return a forbidden-style error. Do not alter the preserved snapshot history on failure.

operations.description:
List immutable seller profile snapshots for one seller account.

This endpoint returns the preserved history of changes made to the seller's public profile, including shop name, shop description, and logo image updates. Each snapshot represents a completed profile edit and records the state before and after the change so sellers and administrators can review storefront identity history for dispute resolution.

The snapshots are read-only and cannot be created, updated, or deleted through this API. Results are scoped to the seller identified by the path parameter and should only include snapshots that belong to that seller profile. Support pagination, sorting by snapshot time, and optional filtering by changed fields or date range to help consumers browse long histories efficiently.

Join the seller profile snapshot records to the owning seller profile through the seller ownership relationship, then return only snapshots belonging to that seller. Support pagination, ordering by snapshot timestamp descending by default, and optional filters such as changed field name and created-at range if those fields are available in the snapshot schema.

Because snapshots are immutable history records, do not allow mutation operations here. Return 404 when the seller does not exist or does not own a profile, and return an empty page when the seller exists but has no snapshots. Ensure authorization allows the owning seller and administrators to read the history, while preventing access to other sellers' snapshots.

operations.description:
Submit a new administrator approval request.

This operation allows an authenticated customer or seller to formally request elevated platform access by providing a reason. The system records the request as pending so it can be reviewed later by a super administrator.

A user can have only one unresolved administrator approval request at a time. If another pending request already exists for the same applicant, the submission is rejected and no new record is created. The stored request preserves the applicant reference, reason, review status, and decision details for governance oversight and future auditing.

Identify the authenticated principal from the session and resolve the applicant account type. Reject unauthenticated callers and reject callers that are not eligible to submit an administrator approval request.

Check mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests for an existing pending request belonging to the same applicant. If one exists, return a duplicate-pending-request error and do not insert a new row.

Validate that the submitted reason is present and non-empty. Create the new approval request with pending status and no reviewer decision data populated yet. Perform the existence check and insert in a transaction to avoid race conditions. Return the created request record after persistence.

requestBody.description: The administrator approval request submission containing the applicant's reason for requesting elevated access.

Immutable snapshot history is stored separately in the administrator approval request snapshot table and is not included in this response. If the record does not exist, the service should return a not-found error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch one row from mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests by id using the approvalRequestId UUID path parameter.
Return the request's current fields: id, administrator_id, reviewer_administrator_id, reason, status, rejection_reason, reviewed_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.
Do not include snapshot rows in the response; snapshots belong to a separate historical operation.
If the record is missing, return not found. If retrieval policy treats deleted rows as inaccessible, honor that policy instead of exposing deleted data.

responseBody.description: The full administrator approval request record containing the current review state and lifecycle timestamps.

parameters.description: The administrator approval request UUID in global scope.
parameters.name: approvalRequestId

operations.description:
Update an administrator approval request with the final review decision.

This operation lets an authorized super administrator process a submitted request for administrator access. The request stores the applicant's reason and the final review outcome so governance history remains traceable after the decision is made.

Only pending requests may be updated. If the request has already been approved or rejected, the system must refuse the update and keep the stored decision unchanged. The request body should contain only the mutable review fields supported by the underlying record, such as the final status and any decision note or rejection reason.

When the request is approved, the applicant is granted regular administrator access. When the request is rejected, the rejection outcome and reason remain preserved for future oversight and audit review.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the administrator approval request by approvalRequestId and verify that it exists. Enforce a pending-only update rule; completed requests must not be overwritten. Apply only the mutable review fields that exist in the actual schema, and keep the applicant's original reason intact.

Perform the update transactionally. If the decision is approved, persist the approval outcome and ensure the applicant receives regular administrator access. If the decision is rejected, persist the rejection outcome and reason so the request remains available as immutable governance history. Do not delete the record or create a replacement record.

Return the updated request entity. If the request does not exist, return a not-found error. If the request is already completed, return a conflict or business-rule error indicating it cannot be processed again. If the caller lacks super-administrator permission, return an authorization error.

responseBody.description: The administrator approval request after the review decision has been saved.

parameters.description: The administrator approval request identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: approvalRequestId

requestBody.description: The mutable review fields used to record the approval or rejection decision for an administrator approval request.

operations.description:
Creates a new authenticated session for an existing customer, seller, or administrator.

The platform validates the submitted credentials, checks that the matched account is allowed to sign in, and then establishes the current authenticated session for that actor. It does not create a new account, and it must not return password secrets or other sensitive credential material.

If authentication fails or the account is not eligible to sign in, the request is rejected and no session is created. A successful response returns the active session context so the client can continue using protected features.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Authenticate the submitted credentials against the registered account records for customers, sellers, and administrators. Determine the actor type from the verified account, then enforce platform eligibility rules before creating a session: reject banned, suspended, rejected, or otherwise unavailable accounts according to actor-specific policy.

On success, create a new session record for the authenticated actor and return the session context. Do not expose password hashes, raw tokens, or any other secret data beyond what the API contract requires. On failure, return an authentication or account-state error and do not create any session row. Preserve the actor identity and role in the response so downstream clients can route the user correctly.

responseBody.description: The newly created authenticated session context for the signed-in actor, including the information needed by the client to continue authenticated use of the platform.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for an existing account. The server uses these values to authenticate the actor and create a new session.

operations.description:
Change the authenticated account owner's password.

This endpoint allows the currently signed-in customer or seller to replace the password associated with their own account. It must only operate on the authenticated principal and must not be used to change another user's credentials or modify unrelated profile, order, address, review, or session data.

The server must verify the current password, validate the new password against the platform password policy, and update the stored credential atomically. If validation fails, the caller is not authenticated, or the current password is incorrect, the request must be rejected and the stored password must remain unchanged.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated principal from the security context and determine whether the caller is a customer or seller account. Validate the supplied current password against the stored hash, then validate the new password against the platform password policy. Reject the request if the caller is not authenticated, does not own the account, or provides an incorrect current password.

Perform the update in a single transaction and modify only the credential fields for the owning account. Do not touch profile records, orders, addresses, wishlists, carts, snapshots, or session tables. If the update fails, return an error and leave the existing password unchanged. Apply the update to the correct account table based on the authenticated principal.

responseBody.description: The updated credential record for the authenticated account owner after a successful password change.

requestBody.description: Password change payload containing the current password and the new password for the authenticated account owner.

operations.description:
Initiate a customer password reset request.

This endpoint creates a new password reset record for a registered customer account and starts the account recovery flow. The system validates that the target account is eligible for recovery, generates a time-limited reset token, and stores the token metadata needed for later verification.

For security, the raw reset token should not be exposed in the normal response. If the target account cannot be recovered or is otherwise ineligible, the request must be rejected without creating a reset record. The operation should be handled atomically so that token generation and persistence succeed together or fail together.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Create a new row in mall_platform_customer_password_resets for the target customer account. Generate a cryptographically secure unique token, set expired_at according to the recovery policy, and leave used_at null on creation. Enforce token uniqueness and treat the entire operation as transactional. If the business rules allow only one active reset token per customer, invalidate or supersede older active records according to the established recovery policy. Do not return the token in the response body or logs. If the customer account does not exist, is banned, or is otherwise ineligible, reject the request without persisting any data.

responseBody.description: Acknowledgment that the password reset request was accepted and the recovery flow has started.

requestBody.description: Password reset initiation payload identifying the customer account to recover and any required delivery target for the reset instructions.

operations.description:
Returns the current approval status of the authenticated seller account.

This endpoint lets a signed-in seller check whether the account is pending, approved, or rejected. If the account is rejected, the response should include the rejection reason so the seller can understand why approval was denied and whether a new registration request is needed.

The approval status is an account-level concern, separate from the public seller profile. Requests without a valid seller session, or requests made by a non-seller identity, must be rejected.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Resolve the current authenticated principal to a seller account and load its current approval status from the seller account record or linked approval workflow state. Return only the seller's own status data. The accepted status values are pending, approved, and rejected. If the status is rejected, include the rejection reason; otherwise return null for the reason if the response model permits it. Reject unauthenticated requests and any request not associated with a seller identity. Do not expose session, password, or unrelated profile fields.

responseBody.description: The authenticated seller account's current approval status and rejection reason when applicable.

operations.description:
Confirms receipt of a shipment and marks every order item in that shipment as delivered.

This operation is customer-facing and applies only to the shipment owned through the customer's order. Delivery confirmation is performed per shipment, not per item, because all items in the same shipment share the same tracking flow and must transition together. Other shipments in the same order remain unchanged.

The response returns the updated shipment so the client can display the resulting tracking and item status information. The server should reject requests for missing shipments, shipments that do not belong to the current customer, and shipments that are no longer eligible for delivery confirmation.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Fetch the shipment by shipmentId and verify that it belongs to an order owned by the authenticated customer. If the shipment does not exist or is not accessible by the caller, return the standard not found or forbidden response.

Perform the confirmation in a single transaction. Update every order item attached to the shipment to delivered status, and update the shipment state so the same shipment cannot be confirmed again. Do not affect other shipments or other items in the order.

If the shipment is already completed, unavailable, or otherwise not eligible for confirmation, return a conflict or unavailable-style error consistent with the service's error conventions. Return the refreshed shipment entity after commit so the client can refresh its view.

responseBody.description: The shipment after delivery confirmation, including its tracking information and associated order items in delivered state.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the shipment to confirm delivery for.
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Force-cancel one order item as an administrative intervention.

This operation allows an administrator with order intervention authority to cancel a single order item when policy enforcement, dispute resolution, or other exceptional circumstances require immediate action. The cancellation applies only to the specified item and does not automatically affect other items in the same order.

When the cancellation succeeds, the system must preserve the historical purchase record, restore stock for the affected variant through an inventory record, and keep any required audit or snapshot history intact. If the item is not eligible for cancellation, the request must fail without changing the order item, related shipment data, or inventory state.

The endpoint is restricted to administrators. It should reject missing, already cancelled, refunded, or otherwise ineligible items, and it must not partially update related records if any validation fails. The response returns the updated order item after the forced cancellation is applied.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Authenticate the caller as an administrator and verify order intervention permission before processing the request. Load the target order item by orderItemId and confirm it exists.

Validate that the item can be force-cancelled under the current business rules. Reject requests for items that are already cancelled, refunded, or otherwise ineligible, and do not modify any related data on failure.

Perform the cancellation in a transaction. Update the order item status to cancelled, create the inventory record that restores the purchased quantity to stock, and preserve the historical trail required for audits and disputes. If the platform stores request or order-item snapshots for state changes, capture the pre/post state as part of the same transaction.

After the item is cancelled, recalculate the parent order status from all order items. If all items are cancelled, mark the order as fully cancelled; otherwise keep the derived mixed/partial status used by the order rules. Do not alter unrelated order items, customer records, or other seller records. If the item belongs to a shipment, keep shipment consistency with the existing shipping rules. Roll back the entire transaction if any step fails.

responseBody.description: The order item after the administrator force-cancellation has been applied, including its updated status and preserved purchase references.

parameters.description: The identifier of the order item to force-cancel (global UUID).
parameters.name: orderItemId

requestBody.description: Administrator force-cancellation request payload used for audit context and dispute handling.

operations.description:
Force-refund a single order item as an administrator intervention.

This endpoint is used for oversight and dispute resolution when an administrator must immediately set one order item to refunded status. It applies only to the specified order item and does not affect unrelated items in the same order unless business rules require derived order status recalculation.

The system must verify that the targeted item exists, belongs to a refundable order context, and is eligible for administrative intervention. When the action succeeds, the item status is changed to refunded, a snapshot is preserved for historical traceability, and inventory restoration is recorded according to the platform’s refund stock rules. If the item is already cancelled or refunded, or if the target cannot be acted on, the request must be rejected without modifying other records.
operations.name: forceRefund
operations.specification:
Load the target order item by its ID and lock it for update. Verify the current administrator has oversight permission to intervene in orders. Confirm the item is not already refunded and that the business rules permit refund intervention for the current item state.

Apply the forced refund as a transactional operation: update the order item status to refunded, create any required immutable snapshot records for the intervention history, and insert the corresponding positive inventory record for the variant if refund stock restoration is required by the platform rules. Recalculate derived order status only if the order summary depends on item states, but do not alter unrelated items.

If the item does not exist, is inaccessible, or is in a terminal state that cannot be refunded again, reject the operation with a business error and leave all data unchanged. The operation must be atomic so that no partial status change or partial inventory restoration is persisted on failure.

responseBody.description: The updated order item after the forced refund has been applied.

parameters.description: The identifier of the order item to force-refund.
parameters.name: orderItemId

operations.description:
Forcibly cancels an order or selected order items under administrator oversight.

This endpoint is reserved for platform administrators who need to intervene in an order for policy enforcement or dispute resolution. The cancellation may apply to the entire order or only to selected items, depending on the request payload, even though ordinary customer cancellation remains item-level and condition-based.

When cancellation is applied, the service must preserve the historical record of the order, update the affected order items, and restore stock for each affected product variant through inventory history records. If the request cancels only part of the order, the remaining items must continue through their normal lifecycle unchanged. After the operation, the overall order status must be recalculated from the item states so the order reflects the combined result of its items.

Validation must reject requests for missing orders, unauthorized callers, ineligible items, or conflicting cancellation scopes. The operation must be atomic: if any targeted item cannot be cancelled, the transaction must roll back and no partial cancellation should be committed.
operations.name: forceCancel
operations.specification:
Authorize the caller as an administrator with order intervention authority before loading or mutating any order data. Fetch the order by orderId and interpret the request body to determine whether the intervention targets the whole order or a subset of items.

Perform all work inside a single transaction. Validate that every targeted item belongs to the order and is eligible for administrative cancellation according to the current item state. Apply the cancellation to each targeted item, restore stock by creating positive inventory records for the corresponding product variants, and preserve the intervention outcome in the platform's snapshot/audit history mechanism so the prior state remains reconstructible.

After all targeted items are processed, recompute the derived order status from the full set of item states. If the order does not exist, the caller lacks authority, any targeted item is not cancellable, or the scope conflicts with the current order state, roll back the transaction and return an appropriate validation or conflict error. Do not allow partial updates.

responseBody.description: The updated order after the forced cancellation has been applied, including the revised item states and recalculated overall status.

parameters.description: The identifier of the order to intervene on.
parameters.name: orderId

requestBody.description: Administrator intervention details indicating whether the full order or specific items should be forcibly cancelled.

operations.description:
Force a refund on an order under administrator oversight.

This endpoint is used for policy enforcement and dispute resolution when an administrator needs to override the normal seller-driven refund flow. The operation affects one order and may apply to all eligible items in that order or to a specified subset, depending on the request payload defined by the domain model.

The service must validate the administrator's intervention permission, confirm that the order exists, and ensure that all targeted items belong to the same order and are eligible for a forced refund. The operation must preserve the historical purchase context and any required snapshot history before the live state changes. If any targeted item fails validation or persistence, the entire request must roll back without partially refunding unrelated items.
operations.name: forceRefund
operations.specification:
Load the order by order_id and verify that the caller is an administrator with order intervention authority. Reject the request with a not-found error if the order does not exist and with a forbidden error if the caller lacks permission.

Determine the target scope from the command body: if explicit order item targets are supplied, validate that each item belongs to the order and can be force-refunded by policy; otherwise, treat the request as an order-wide forced refund over all eligible items. For every targeted item, write any required snapshot record before mutating the live row, update the item status to refunded, restore stock by creating the appropriate positive inventory record, and trigger the refund settlement workflow exactly once per item.

Use a single database transaction for the full operation. Do not modify unrelated order items. If any item is in an ineligible state or any downstream persistence step fails, roll back the transaction and return a domain error explaining the failure condition.

responseBody.description: The updated order after the forced refund has been applied, including the current item states and preserved order context.

parameters.description: The order identifier (UUID) for the administrator intervention.
parameters.name: orderId

requestBody.description: Administrator refund command for the selected order scope.

operations.description:
Create a seller-specific shipment for eligible order items.

This endpoint groups one or more order items from the same seller into a single shipment and stores the shared carrier name and tracking number for that delivery package. It is used during seller fulfillment after the seller selects items that still need shipping.

The request must only include order items owned by the authenticated seller and all selected items must belong to the same seller. Items that are already shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, completed, or otherwise unavailable for shipping must be rejected. If any selected item is invalid or the shipment is no longer available, the entire request fails and no shipment is created.

The created shipment is the customer-visible delivery record used in order details and order history. All included items must be associated with the shipment in the same transaction so the shipment grouping and item shipping status remain consistent.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated seller owns every requested order item and that every item is eligible for shipping. Enforce that all selected items belong to one seller only and reject any request that mixes sellers or references items that are already shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, or otherwise unavailable.

Create the shipment and its shipment-item links in a single transaction. Persist the carrier name and tracking number on the shipment record, then insert one shipment-item association for each included order item. Update each included order item to shipped in the same transaction so the shipment and order-item states cannot diverge.

If the schema includes additional metadata columns such as timestamps, populate them only when they actually exist in the loaded schema. On validation failure, unavailable item detection, or concurrency conflict, roll back the transaction and return a clear error indicating that the shipment cannot be created because the selected items are unavailable or already completed.

responseBody.description: The newly created shipment with its tracking information and included order items.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation data including the selected order item identifiers and the shared carrier and tracking information.

operations.description:
Retrieve the shared tracking details for a single shipment.

A shipment is the platform's delivery unit, so this endpoint returns the carrier name and tracking number that apply to the entire package. The same tracking information is used for every order item included in that shipment.

This data is used in the customer order detail view to follow delivery progress for grouped items. If the shipment does not exist, the service must return a not found error. If the caller is not authorized to view the shipment, the service must return an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Look up the shipment by shipmentId and verify that the caller is allowed to view it according to ownership and role-based access rules. Return the shipment-level tracking information, including carrier name and tracking number, and keep the response aligned with the shipment delivery unit concept. Do not introduce item-level tracking differences because all items in the shipment share the same tracking data. Return 404 when the shipment is missing and 403 when access is denied.

responseBody.description: Shipment-level tracking information for one delivery package, including the shared carrier name and tracking number used to follow the shipment.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the shipment whose tracking details are being retrieved.

operations.description:
Returns the order items assigned to a shipment.

This endpoint is used by shipment detail and order history screens to show which purchased items were packed together, along with the item-level purchase context needed for tracking and delivery confirmation.

The shipment is always treated as a seller-scoped package, so the returned items must all belong to the same shipment and therefore the same seller. If the shipment does not exist or the requester is not allowed to view it, the service must return the platform's standard not-found or authorization response. The endpoint does not infer items from the order; it only exposes explicit shipment-item membership stored by the system.
operations.name: getByShipmentid
operations.specification:
Load the shipment identified by shipmentId, then verify the current actor is permitted to view it according to shipment visibility rules. Query mall_platform_shipment_items for rows belonging to that shipment and join them to mall_platform_order_items so the response can include the purchase-line context needed by shipment and order-detail screens.

Return only items explicitly linked to the shipment. Preserve any stored ordering if the service layer or database maintains one. Do not merge items from other shipments, and do not infer additional items from the parent order. If the shipment is valid but has no items, return an empty collection. If the shipment is missing, return 404. If access is denied, return the standard authorization response.

responseBody.description: The shipment's order items, returned as a shipment-scoped summary collection for detail and tracking views.

parameters.description: The shipment identifier (UUID scope) used to load the shipment item membership.

operations.description:
Records the seller’s decision for a cancellation request on a specific order item.

This operation applies to one cancellation request that belongs to one paid order item that has not been shipped yet. The decision is made at item level, so other items in the same order are not affected by this action.

When the seller approves the request, the order item is cancelled and the service layer must apply the downstream business effects for that item, including inventory restoration and any refund processing required by the platform workflow. When the seller rejects the request, the order item remains unchanged and the request is closed with the rejection outcome.

Every successful decision must preserve an immutable request snapshot so the pre-decision and post-decision state can be reviewed later for dispute resolution. The request must be rejected when the referenced records do not match, the request is not in a reviewable state, or the caller is not authorized to decide for the item.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the cancellation request by cancellationRequestId and verify that it belongs to the orderItemId provided in the route. If the request is missing or the association does not match, return not found.

Authorize the caller as the seller of the order item, or as an administrator only if the authorization layer explicitly permits administrative oversight on cancellation decisions. The request must still be pending or otherwise reviewable; if it is already decided, return conflict.

Apply the decision atomically in a transaction. Update the cancellation request status and reviewer outcome fields, then create an immutable cancellation request snapshot capturing the state before the change and the state after the change. If the decision is approval, trigger the item-level cancellation workflow so the order item becomes cancelled and inventory is restored through a positive inventory record. If the decision is rejection, leave the order item unchanged and persist the rejection outcome only.

operations.description:
Records the seller’s decision for a cancellation request on a specific order item.

This operation applies to one cancellation request that belongs to one paid order item that has not been shipped yet. The decision is made at item level, so other items in the same order are not affected by this action.

When the seller approves the request, the order item is cancelled and the service layer must apply the downstream business effects for that item, including inventory restoration and any refund processing required by the platform workflow. When the seller rejects the request, the order item remains unchanged and the request is closed with the rejection outcome.

Every successful decision must preserve an immutable request snapshot so the pre-decision and post-decision state can be reviewed later for dispute resolution. The request must be rejected when the referenced records do not match, the request is not in a reviewable state, or the caller is not authorized to decide for the item.

Apply the decision atomically in a transaction. Update the cancellation request status and reviewer outcome fields, then create an immutable cancellation request snapshot capturing the state before the change and the state after the change. If the decision is approval, trigger the item-level cancellation workflow so the order item becomes cancelled and inventory is restored through a positive inventory record. If the decision is rejection, leave the order item unchanged and persist the rejection outcome only.

This endpoint returns the immutable variant-state records captured for the requested snapshot so clients can reconstruct the SKU code, option values, price override, and availability that existed when the product snapshot was created.

operations.description:
Returns the immutable snapshot history for a specific order item.

This endpoint exposes preserved historical records for the order item so customers, sellers, and administrators can review the purchase context as it existed at each recorded change. Order item snapshots are retained for dispute resolution, auditability, and historical reconstruction, and they remain available even if the source order item or related source records have since changed or been removed.

The response is scoped to the specified order item and contains only snapshots that belong to that parent. Because snapshot history can grow over time, the result is paginated. If the parent order item does not exist, the service should return not found. If the caller is not allowed to view the preserved history, the service should return forbidden.

Resolve the parent order item by orderItemId and verify access according to the caller's role and ownership rules. Query mall_platform_order_item_snapshots for rows linked to that order item, ordering newest first by the snapshot timestamp or creation timestamp defined by the schema. Return a paginated summary list and do not allow mutation because snapshots are immutable by business rule.

If the parent order item does not exist, return not found. If the caller lacks permission to view the history, return forbidden. Do not reconstruct, update, or delete snapshot rows. If the schema contains related preserved fields for product or seller context, expose them only through the snapshot summary type, not through any write behavior. Follow standard pagination and sorting behavior for list-style retrieval of historical data.

operations.description:
Record a super administrator decision for a pending administrator approval request and return the updated request.

This endpoint lets a privileged reviewer approve or reject an administrator approval request submitted by a customer or seller. The request keeps the original applicant reason together with the reviewer outcome so the governance history remains traceable.

The operation applies to exactly one approval request identified by `approvalRequestId`. Requests that do not exist, are already finalized, or are attempted by a caller without the required super-administrator privilege must be rejected. When the decision is accepted, the platform preserves the final status and reviewer outcome for future oversight and dispute review.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Look up the administrator approval request by approvalRequestId and verify it exists. Enforce super-administrator authorization before allowing the decision flow. Reject any request that is not still pending to prevent duplicate finalization.

Apply the decision in a single transaction. Persist the reviewer outcome, update the request status to approved or rejected, and preserve the applicant reason and decision details as governance history. If the request is approved, promote the requesting account to a regular administrator according to the platform rules. If the request is rejected, keep the applicant account unchanged and store the rejection outcome for later review.

Return the updated request after commit. Use 404 for missing requests, 403 for insufficient privileges, and a conflict or validation failure when the request cannot be finalized in its current state.

operations.description:
Submit a new administrator approval request for a customer or seller account.

This endpoint creates a fresh governance request when an existing user wants to be considered for administrator access again. The submitted request stores the applicant’s reason for seeking elevated access and begins in a pending state so that super administrators can review it later.

A resubmission must not alter any previously approved or rejected administrator request. If the applicant is not eligible, the reason is missing, or the system cannot create a new request record, the operation must fail without changing existing governance history.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new row in mall_platform_administrator_approval_requests with a pending status and the applicant-provided reason. Validate that the request is being made by an existing customer or seller account permitted to seek administrator access, and reject attempts from unavailable account states. If the domain model distinguishes applicant identity fields, map them from the create DTO and do not derive them from any previous completed request.

Before insertion, ensure there is no conflicting pending administrator approval request for the same applicant if the business rules prohibit duplicates. Never update a completed request; resubmission must always create a new record to preserve the approval/rejection history. Return the created request after persistence, including its current status and any review metadata that exists at creation time.
