id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.id. Expose the UUID primary key as the shipment identifier.

carrierName.description:
The shipping carrier name.

This identifies the carrier responsible for transporting the package.
carrierName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.carrier_name. Expose the shipment carrier name exactly as stored.

trackingNumber.description:
The shipment tracking number.

This number is used to follow the package with the carrier.
trackingNumber.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.tracking_number. Expose the carrier-issued tracking number for the shipment.

trackingUrl.description:
The optional carrier tracking URL.

When present, this opens the carrier's tracking page for the shipment.
trackingUrl.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.tracking_url. Preserve null when no tracking URL is stored; otherwise expose the stored URL string.

status.description:
The current shipment status.

This indicates the package's delivery progress, such as preparing, shipped, delivered, or cancelled.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.status. Expose the shipment status exactly as stored in the database.

shippedAt.description:
The time the shipment was handed to the carrier.

This value is null until the package has been dispatched.
shippedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.shipped_at. Preserve null until the shipment is handed to the carrier; otherwise expose the stored timestamp.

deliveredAt.description:
The time the shipment was confirmed delivered.

This value is null until the package reaches delivered status.
deliveredAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.delivered_at. Preserve null until delivery is confirmed; otherwise expose the stored timestamp.

seller.description:
The seller responsible for this shipment.

This is shown as a seller summary so clients can display the merchant context for the package.
seller.x-autobe-specification: Join mall_platform_shipments.mall_platform_seller_id to mall_platform_sellers.id and return IMallPlatformSeller.ISummary as the seller summary relation. This is a read-side relation mapping, not the raw foreign key column.

order.description:
The order associated with this shipment.

This is shown as an order summary so clients can display which purchase the package belongs to.
order.x-autobe-specification: Join mall_platform_shipments.mall_platform_order_id to mall_platform_orders.id and return IMallPlatformOrder.ISummary as the order summary relation. This is a read-side relation mapping, not the raw foreign key column.

createdAt.description:
The time the shipment record was created.

This timestamp helps consumers identify when the shipment entry was first recorded.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.created_at. Expose the creation timestamp in ISO date-time format.

updatedAt.description:
The time the shipment record was last updated.

This timestamp reflects the most recent change to the shipment record.
updatedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.updated_at. Expose the last update timestamp in ISO date-time format.

deletedAt.description:
The time the shipment was soft-deleted.

This value is null for active shipments and populated only for logically removed records.
deletedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_shipments.deleted_at. Preserve null for active shipments and expose the stored soft-delete timestamp when logically removed.

IMallPlatformShipment.IInvert.description:
Shipment tracking details for one delivery package.

This schema represents the read-only shipment view used by customer, seller, and administrator tracking endpoints. It includes the shipment's core tracking fields, lifecycle timestamps, and linked seller and order summaries needed to display package-level tracking information.

The response is intentionally shipment-level rather than item-level. Item membership is excluded because every item in the shipment shares the same carrier and tracking data, and the item list is exposed elsewhere.
IMallPlatformShipment.IInvert.x-autobe-specification: Map this read DTO directly from mall_platform_shipments as the shipment tracking/detail view. Expose scalar shipment fields as direct mappings from their snake_case columns. Expose seller and order as read-side relation summaries joined from mall_platform_seller_id → mall_platform_sellers.id and mall_platform_order_id → mall_platform_orders.id. Keep all nullable database fields nullable in the DTO and preserve ISO date-time formatting for timestamp fields. Do not include shipmentItems because this DTO is shipment-level tracking data, not item membership data.

orderItemIds.description:
The order items to include in the forced refund.

Provide zero or more order item UUIDs to narrow the administrator action to selected items within the target order. If omitted, the system applies the forced refund to all eligible items.

The server verifies ownership and eligibility for each listed item before executing the refund.
orderItemIds.x-autobe-specification: Optional array of order item UUIDs to include in the forced refund for the order identified by the path parameter. When present, each UUID must be validated against the target order and forced-refund eligibility before any state changes occur. When absent, the service applies the refund to all eligible items in the order. Do not persist this field; it is request-only input.

IMallPlatformOrder.IForceRefund.description:
Administrator command payload for selecting the scope of a forced refund.

Use this body to limit the administrator action to specific order items within the target order. If orderItemIds is omitted, the forced refund applies to all eligible items in that order.

This payload is execution input only. The server resolves the order identity from the path, validates eligibility, and records any required snapshots during processing.
IMallPlatformOrder.IForceRefund.x-autobe-specification: This schema is the request body for the administrator force-refund operation on a specific order. The optional orderItemIds array narrows the refund to specific order items within the order identified by the path parameter; if omitted, the service must apply the forced refund to all eligible items in that order. The payload is not persisted and does not map to a database column or relation; it exists only to instruct validation and execution of the refund workflow, including item ownership checks and eligibility checks before any mutation occurs.

IMallPlatformAdministratorApprovalReques.description:
An update payload for recording the final review decision on an administrator approval request.

This payload is used by an authorized super administrator to approve or reject a pending request. It includes only the fields that may change during review and does not expose the applicant's original reason or identity.

If the request is rejected, a rejection reason should be provided. If the request is approved, the rejection reason is typically omitted or null. Reviewer metadata and the review timestamp may be stored by the backend as part of the same update transaction.
IMallPlatformAdministratorApprovalReques.x-autobe-specification: Maps the mutable review fields for an administrator approval request. The backend should apply this payload only to pending requests and preserve the applicant reason and identity. Reviewer metadata and review timestamp may be recorded during the same transaction when available.

id.description:
The unique identifier of this cancellation request snapshot.

This value identifies one immutable historical record and is used to reference the snapshot in API responses and related lookups.

snapshotStatus.description:
The cancellation request status preserved when this snapshot was recorded.

This reflects the request state at the historical moment captured by the snapshot, not the current live request state.

reviewResult.description:
The reviewer outcome preserved in this snapshot, if one was recorded.

This field shows the decision or result associated with the request at the time of capture and may be absent when the request had not yet been reviewed.
reviewResult.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_cancellation_request_snapshots.review_result. Nullable in the database, so the DTO allows null.

reason.description:
The cancellation reason or reviewer note preserved in this snapshot, if available.

This text captures the reason that was recorded when the snapshot was created and is retained for audit and dispute review.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_cancellation_request_snapshots.reason. Nullable in the database, so the DTO allows null.

changedAt.description:
The business time when the captured cancellation request state became effective.

This timestamp marks when the preserved state represented by the snapshot should be considered active in the business timeline.

createdAt.description:
The time when this snapshot record was created.

This is the storage creation timestamp for the immutable history entry.

updatedAt.description:
The time when this snapshot record was last updated in storage.

This is an audit timestamp for the immutable record and indicates the most recent persistence update, if any.

deletedAt.description:
The soft-delete timestamp for this snapshot record, if one exists.

Snapshot rows are normally retained permanently, so this field is expected to remain null in standard operation.
deletedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from mall_platform_cancellation_request_snapshots.deleted_at. Nullable in the database, so the DTO allows null.

cancellationRequest.description:
The cancellation request that this snapshot belongs to.

This nested summary reference lets consumers inspect the live cancellation request associated with the preserved historical snapshot.
cancellationRequest.x-autobe-specification: Resolve the belonged relation from mall_platform_cancellation_request_snapshots.cancellationRequest to mall_platform_cancellation_requests and expose it as IMallPlatformCancellationRequest.ISummary.

IMallPlatformCancellationRequestSnapshot.description:
Immutable cancellation request snapshot history entry.

This summary represents one preserved point-in-time state of a cancellation request, including the stored status, reviewer outcome, reason text, linked cancellation request, and audit timestamps. It is intended for historical review and dispute resolution and reflects the request exactly as it was recorded when the snapshot was created.
IMallPlatformCancellationRequestSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: Read-only summary DTO for immutable cancellation request snapshots. Map the snapshot table columns directly to the DTO properties id, snapshotStatus, reviewResult, reason, changedAt, createdAt, updatedAt, and deletedAt. Map the belonged cancellationRequest relation to IMallPlatformCancellationRequest.ISummary, resolved from mall_platform_cancellation_request_id. The raw foreign key column is intentionally excluded because the consumer-facing representation is the nested cancellation request summary. This DTO is used for historical review and dispute resolution and must preserve the immutable snapshot state exactly as stored.

mall_platform_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer account to recover.

Provide the UUID of the customer account that should receive a password reset record. The server uses this value to create the recovery entry and associate it with the matching customer account.
mall_platform_customer_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to mall_platform_customer_password_resets.mall_platform_customer_id. This UUID identifies the customer account that will receive the password reset record. The server uses it to create and associate the recovery entry; no nested customer object is accepted in this request body.

IMallPlatformCustomerPasswordReset.ICrea.description:
Password reset initiation payload for a customer account.

This request identifies the customer account that should receive a password reset record. The server creates the recovery entry and manages the token, expiration, usage state, and audit timestamps internally.
IMallPlatformCustomerPasswordReset.ICrea.x-autobe-specification: This DTO creates a customer password reset record in mall_platform_customer_password_resets. The client supplies only the customer account UUID via mall_platform_customer_id. The server uses that value to create the reset row, generate the secure token, compute expired_at, initialize used_at as null, and manage created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at internally. The customer relation is derived from mall_platform_customer_id and is not sent as a nested object in the request body.

scope.description:
Selects whether the administrator cancels the whole order or only specific order items.

Use wholeOrder to apply the intervention to every eligible item on the order referenced by the URL path. Use selectedItems to cancel only the order items listed in orderItemIds.
scope.x-autobe-specification: Use this field to choose the scope of the administrator force-cancel action for the order identified by the URL path. wholeOrder means cancel every eligible item in the referenced order. selectedItems means cancel only the order items listed in orderItemIds after verifying each item belongs to the target order and is eligible for cancellation. This value is not persisted to mall_platform_orders and has no database mapping.

orderItemIds.description:
The order item UUIDs to cancel when only selected items are targeted.

This field is used only when scope is selectedItems and must contain UUIDs for order items that belong to the order in the URL path.
orderItemIds.x-autobe-specification: Provide the UUIDs of the order items to cancel when scope is selectedItems. Each UUID must reference an order item that belongs to the order identified by the URL path and is eligible for administrative cancellation. The list must contain unique UUIDs and is ignored when scope is wholeOrder. This value is not persisted to mall_platform_orders and has no database mapping.

IMallPlatformOrder.ICreate.description:
Administrator intervention payload for forcibly cancelling an existing order.

Use this request body with the administrator force-cancel endpoint to choose whether the cancellation applies to the entire order or only selected order items. The order itself is identified by the URL path, so this body only carries cancellation scope and item-selection input.
IMallPlatformOrder.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: This schema is the administrator-only request body for the force-cancel order endpoint. It does not create or update a mall_platform_orders row. The URL path supplies the target orderId; this body supplies cancellation control input only. scope selects whether the operation applies to the entire referenced order or only to a chosen subset of its items. orderItemIds is used only when scope is selectedItems and must contain UUIDs for items that belong to the target order and are eligible for administrative cancellation. Both fields are request-time control values and map to no persisted order columns or relations.

decision.description:
The approval or rejection decision for the cancellation request.

Set this field to indicate how the pending request should be resolved. The server uses the value to update the request and record the final outcome.
decision.x-autobe-specification: Interpret this field as the approve/reject command for the cancellation decision workflow. The service layer combines it with the route parameters and authenticated reviewer to finalize the request, update persisted state, and write the immutable snapshot. Because the stored record uses status and review metadata instead of a decision column, this field has no direct database mapping.

reviewerNote.description:
An optional note from the reviewer.

Use this to explain the approval or rejection decision, add context, or leave a short internal comment. It may be omitted when no note is needed.
reviewerNote.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to mall_platform_cancellation_requests.reviewer_note. Persist the note when provided; store null when omitted. This field is optional and is used only as supporting context for the reviewer’s decision.

IMallPlatformCancellationRequest.IDecisi.description:
Cancellation request decision payload.

Use this body to approve or reject a pending cancellation request for a specific order item, and optionally attach a reviewer note. The route identifies the request target while authentication identifies the acting reviewer.
IMallPlatformCancellationRequest.IDecisi.x-autobe-specification: This request body carries only the user-entered inputs needed to decide a pending cancellation request. The decision field is a workflow command consumed by the service layer to approve or reject the target request; it does not map to a stored column and instead drives server-side updates to status, review_result, reviewed_at, reviewer_id, and snapshot history. The reviewerNote field maps directly to the persisted reviewer_note column and should be stored as the reviewer’s optional explanatory note. Route parameters and authentication context supply the order-item scope and reviewer identity, so they must not appear in this DTO.

IMallPlatformSellerProfile.ISummary.description:
A compact seller profile summary.

This object represents the current public shop profile for one seller account. It is used in browsing, seller profile pages, and snapshot-related references, and includes the seller account relation together with the shop name, shop description, logo image URI, and lifecycle timestamps.

The summary contains only the live profile state stored in the database. Historical edits are preserved separately in seller profile snapshots and are not included here.
IMallPlatformSellerProfile.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Map directly from mall_platform_seller_profiles. Expose id, shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_uri, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at from the row. Resolve seller_account_id through the sellerAccount relation and expose it as IMallPlatformSellerAccount.ISummary. Do not include sellerProfileSnapshots in this summary view.

IMallPlatformCancellationRequest.ISummar.description:
A summary view of a cancellation request for one order item.

This object represents the current live state of a cancellation request, including the requested reason, review outcome, reviewer note, and lifecycle timestamps. It is used for scoped retrieval and list views where consumers need the active request state without the full immutable snapshot history.
IMallPlatformCancellationRequest.ISummar.x-autobe-specification: Map id, reason, status, reviewed_at, review_result, reviewer_note, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at directly from mall_platform_cancellation_requests. Resolve mall_platform_cancellation_requests.mall_platform_order_item_id to orderItem as IMallPlatformOrderItem.ISummary. Resolve mall_platform_cancellation_requests.reviewer_id to reviewer as IMallPlatformAdministrator.ISummary when present, otherwise null. Do not expose raw foreign-key scalar properties or the snapshots collection in the summary DTO.

text: The interface phase is already complete, so I can proceed to the E2E test generation phase now. I’ll generate test suites for the API contract and the main business flows described in the requirements.

instruction:
Create comprehensive end-to-end test functions for the e-commerce shopping mall platform API interfaces based on the following requirements.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

I want to create an e-commerce shopping mall platform.

## Customer Account

- This platform requires registration to use any features (no guest browsing)
- Customers sign up with email and password
- Customers log in with email and password
- Customers can change their password
- Customers can delete their account
- When a customer deletes their account:
  - Their profile information is deleted
  - Their orders and order history are preserved (for seller records and legal purposes)
  - Their reviews are preserved but shown as "deleted user"

## Customer Profile

- Each customer has a profile with: display name and phone number
- Customers can edit their display name and phone number

## Address Management

- Customers can add multiple shipping addresses
- Each address has: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country
- Customers can edit their addresses
- Customers can delete their addresses
- Customers can set one address as the default shipping address

## Seller Account

- Sellers sign up with email and password
- Sellers log in with email and password
- Sellers can change their password
- Seller accounts require administrator approval before they can sell
- Sellers can view their approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- If rejected, sellers can view the rejection reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Sellers can delete their account only if:
  - They have no pending orders (paid or shipped status)
  - They have no pending cancellation or refund requests
- When a seller deletes their account:
  - Their products are deleted from listings
  - Order history and snapshots are preserved
  - Their shop name in past orders is preserved

## Seller Profile

- Each seller has a profile with: shop name, shop description, and logo image
- Sellers can edit their shop name, description, and logo
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can view seller profiles

## Categories

- Products are organized into categories
- Categories can have subcategories (one level of nesting only)
- Each category has: name and description
- Categories are created and managed by administrators only
- Customers can browse the list of all categories
- Customers can view products within a category

## Snapshot Principle

- This is a platform where money is exchanged, so all data modifications must be recorded
- Whenever editable data is modified, a snapshot is created to preserve the previous state
- Snapshots record: when the change was made, what was changed, and the values before and after
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Snapshots can be viewed by relevant parties (owners, administrators) for dispute resolution

**Product Snapshot Structure**
- When a product is edited, a product snapshot is created
- The product snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category, base price, images)
- The product snapshot also includes snapshots of all variants at that moment (product-snapshot → product-snapshot-SKU)
- This preserves the complete state of a product and its variants at any point in time

**Snapshot applies to:**
- Products (all fields including images)
- Product variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Seller profiles (shop name, description, logo)
- Order items (product, variant, and seller profile at time of purchase)
- Reviews (rating, text content)
- Cancellation requests (reason, status changes)
- Refund requests (reason, status changes)

## Products

- Sellers can create products
- Every product has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (required)
  - Category (required, can select a subcategory)
  - Base price (required)
- Products belong to the seller who created them
- Sellers can edit their own products
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete their own products only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for any variant of the product
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant of the product
- Deleting a product also deletes all its variants and inventory records
- Deleted products no longer appear in search or category listings
- Sellers can view snapshots of their own products
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Snapshots are preserved even after product deletion

## Product Images

- Sellers can upload multiple images for each product
- Images can be reordered (first image is the main/thumbnail image)
- Sellers can delete images from their products
- Image changes are included in product snapshots

## Product Variants (SKU)

- A product can have multiple variants
- Each variant represents a specific combination of options (e.g., "Red / Large", "Blue / Small")
- Each variant has:
  - SKU code (unique identifier, required)
  - Option values (e.g., color: "Red", size: "Large")
  - Price (can override the base price, optional)
  - Stock quantity (required, starts at 0)
- Sellers can add variants to their products
- Sellers can edit variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Every variant edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete variants only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for that variant
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for that variant
- A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable
- Products with no variants are visible in search but shown as "unavailable"

## Inventory Management

- Each variant has its own stock quantity
- Stock quantity is managed through inventory history records (not snapshots)
- Each inventory record contains: quantity change (positive for restocking, negative for orders/adjustments), reason, and timestamp
- Current stock is calculated by summing all inventory records
- Sellers can add inventory (restock) with a quantity and reason
- Sellers can subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with a quantity and reason
- Order placement automatically creates a negative inventory record
- Order cancellation/refund automatically creates a positive inventory record
- Sellers can view the full inventory history of each variant
- When stock reaches 0, the variant is shown as "out of stock"
- Out of stock variants cannot be added to cart

## Product Search

- Customers can search products by name
- Search results show products from all sellers
- Search results are paginated
- Customers can filter search results by:
  - Category
  - Price range (minimum and maximum)
  - In-stock only
- Customers can sort search results by:
  - Newest first
  - Price (low to high)
  - Price (high to low)

## Product Listing

- When viewing a list of products (search results, category page), each product shows:
  - Main image (thumbnail)
  - Name
  - Base price (or price range if variants have different prices)
  - Seller shop name
  - Average rating (if reviews exist)

## Product Detail Page

- Customers can view a single product's full details
- The page shows:
  - All images
  - Name and description
  - Category
  - Seller shop name (links to seller profile)
  - All available variants with prices and stock status
  - Average rating and total review count
  - All reviews

## Wishlist

- Customers can add products to their wishlist
- Customers can view their wishlist
- The wishlist is paginated
- Wishlist shows products (not specific variants)
- Customers can remove products from their wishlist
- If a product is deleted by the seller, it is automatically removed from all wishlists

## Shopping Cart

- Customers can add variants to their cart (must select a specific variant, not just a product)
- When adding to cart, customers specify the quantity
- If the same variant is already in the cart, the quantities are combined (not added as a separate line)
- Customers can view their cart
- Cart shows each item with: product name, variant options, price, quantity, and subtotal
- Customers can change the quantity of items in their cart
- Customers can remove items from their cart
- Cart shows the total price of all items
- If a variant's stock is less than the cart quantity, a warning is shown
- If a variant is deleted or out of stock, it is marked as unavailable in the cart

## Checkout

- Customers can proceed to checkout from their cart
- Unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Customers must select a shipping address (or use default)
- Customers can review the order summary before placing the order:
  - List of items with prices
  - Shipping address
  - Total price
- Once an order is placed, the shipping address cannot be changed

## Payment

- After reviewing, customers confirm and place the order
- Payment is processed (assume external payment gateway integration)
- Payment can succeed or fail
- If payment fails, the order is not created and customers can retry
- If payment succeeds, the order is created

## Order Creation

- When an order is placed successfully:
  - Stock quantities are decreased for each purchased variant
  - Items are removed from the customer's cart
  - An order record is created
  - Each purchased variant becomes an order item with status "paid"
  - A snapshot of each purchased product and variant is saved with the order item (preserves product name, description, variant options, and price at the time of purchase)
  - A snapshot of each seller's profile is saved with the order item (preserves shop name and logo at the time of purchase)

## Order Structure

- An order contains one or more order items
- Each order item represents a purchased product variant with a quantity
- If a customer buys 3 of the same variant, it becomes one order item with quantity 3
- Order items can be from different sellers
- Each order item has its own status
- Each order item can be individually cancelled or refunded
- Order items are grouped into shipments when shipped (see Shipping and Tracking)

## Order History

- Customers can view a list of all their orders
- The list is paginated and sorted by newest first
- Each order in the list shows: order number, date, total price, and overall order status
- Customers can view the full details of an order:
  - List of items with: product name, variant, quantity, price, and item status
  - Shipping address
  - List of shipments with tracking information (each shipment shows which items are included)

## Order Status

**Order Item Status**
- Each item in an order has its own status
- Item statuses:
  - Paid: payment completed, waiting for seller to ship
  - Shipped: seller has shipped the item
  - Delivered: item has been delivered
  - Cancelled: item was cancelled
  - Refunded: item was refunded

**Order Status**
- The overall order status is derived from its items
- If all items are paid → order is "paid"
- If any item is shipped (and none delivered yet) → order is "shipped"
- If all items are delivered → order is "delivered"
- If all items are cancelled → order is "cancelled"
- If all items are refunded → order is "refunded"
- Mixed states (e.g., some delivered, some refunded) → order is "partially completed"

## Shipping and Tracking

**Shipment Concept**
- A shipment is a package sent by a seller
- A shipment can contain one or more order items from the same seller
- Different sellers always ship separately (different shipments)
- A seller can choose to ship items individually or bundle multiple items into one shipment

**Shipping Process**
- Sellers can view order items for their products that need shipping
- When shipping, sellers select one or more of their items to include in a shipment
- Sellers enter tracking information for the shipment (carrier name, tracking number)
- All items in the same shipment share the same tracking information
- When a shipment is created, all items in it change to status "shipped"

**Delivery Confirmation**
- Customers can view tracking information for each shipment
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment (not per item)
- When the customer confirms delivery, all items in that shipment change to status "delivered"
- If the customer does not confirm, items automatically change to "delivered" after 14 days from shipping

## Order Cancellation

- Cancellation is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request cancellation for individual items with status "paid" (not yet shipped)
- Cancellation requests include a reason (text)
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the cancellation request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is cancelled and refund is processed for that item only
- Cancelled items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order continue processing normally
- If all items in an order are cancelled, the entire order status becomes "cancelled"

## Refund Requests

- Refund is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request a refund for individual items with status "delivered"
- Refund requests include a reason (text)
- Refund can be requested within 7 days of that item being delivered
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the refund request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is refunded
- Refunded items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order are unaffected
- If all items in an order are refunded, the entire order status becomes "refunded"

## Reviews and Ratings

- Customers can write a review for products they have purchased
- A review can only be written after that item's status is "delivered"
- Customers can write one review per product per order
- Each review has:
  - Rating (1 to 5 stars, required)
  - Text content (optional)
- Reviews are displayed on the product detail page
- Reviews are sorted by newest first
- Customers can edit their own reviews
- Every review edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can delete their own reviews (but snapshots are preserved)
- Product's average rating is calculated from all non-deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard

- Sellers can view a summary of their shop:
  - Total number of products
  - Total number of order items (for their products)
  - Number of pending cancellation requests
  - Number of pending refund requests
- Sellers can view a list of all order items for their products
- Sellers can filter order items by status

## Administrator System

**Becoming an Administrator**
- Any user (customer or seller) can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

**Administrator Grades**
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

**Seller Management**
- Administrators can view the list of pending seller approvals
- Administrators can approve or reject seller registrations
- When rejecting, administrators must provide a reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Administrators can suspend seller accounts
- When a seller is suspended:
  - Their products are hidden from search and category listings
  - Their products cannot be purchased
  - They can still process existing orders (ship items, respond to cancellation/refund requests)
  - They cannot create new products or edit existing products
- Administrators can unsuspend seller accounts (products become visible again)

**Category Management**
- Administrators can create categories and subcategories
- Administrators can edit category names and descriptions
- Administrators can delete categories (products in deleted categories become uncategorized)

**Product Oversight**
- Administrators can view all products on the platform
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Administrators can delete any product (for policy violations)

**Order Oversight**
- Administrators can view all orders on the platform
- Administrators can force-cancel individual items or entire orders (refunds the customer, restores stock)
- Administrators can force-refund individual items or entire orders

**User Management**
- Administrators can view all customer accounts
- Administrators can ban customers (banned customers cannot log in)
- Administrators can unban customers
- Administrators can view all seller accounts
- Administrators can ban sellers (banned sellers cannot log in, existing orders remain)

In scenarios with multiple actors, the test agent needs to authenticate as different users to simulate real-world multi-user interactions.
This login operation ensures proper session management and authorization context switching, allowing the test to validate permissions, access controls, and business logic that span across different user actors within a single test scenario.
This login operation may be required for user actor swapping between multiple actors.

Actor switching authentication:
This login operation (post /mallPlatform/auth/customer/login) enables dynamic user actor switching during test execution for the 'customer' actor.
In scenarios with multiple actors, the test agent needs to authenticate as different users to simulate real-world multi-user interactions.
This login operation ensures proper session management and authorization context switching, allowing the test to validate permissions, access controls, and business logic that span across different user actors within a single test scenario.
This login operation may be required for user actor swapping between multiple actors.
Authenticate as a customer to establish a non-administrator actor for the access-control check.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_admin_only_access

scenario.draft: Log in as an administrator through the join flow, then retrieve an existing seller account by UUID and verify the response returns the complete seller account detail plus its linked seller profile. The test should validate that the account state fields are returned exactly as stored, including approval status, rejection reason, suspension timestamp, deletion timestamp, createdAt, and updatedAt, and that the nested sellerProfile contains the shop name, description, logo URI, and its own timestamps. Confirm the linked profile belongs to the same seller account and that password data is never exposed in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because this seller-account detail endpoint is restricted to administrators.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_detail_retrieve

scenario.draft: Authenticate as an administrator, then retrieve a seller account that is in a non-active moderation or lifecycle state such as rejected, suspended, or soft-deleted. Verify that the response preserves the stored seller account state without inferring values from the seller profile, and that nullable fields such as rejectionReason, suspendedAt, deletedAt, and sellerProfile.logoImageUri remain null when not set. The response should still include the linked seller profile so administrators can inspect storefront identity alongside the account status.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because viewing seller lifecycle state is an administrator-only capability.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_detail_preserves_lifecycle_state

scenario.draft: Authenticate as an administrator, then request a seller account UUID that does not correspond to any stored seller account. Verify the endpoint responds with a not-found outcome and does not return a partial seller record, a fallback profile, or any unrelated account data. This confirms the administrator lookup uses the seller account record as the authoritative source and handles missing records cleanly.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because the endpoint requires administrator authorization even when the seller account does not exist.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_detail_not_found

scenario.draft: Verify that a freshly registered seller, authenticated in the seller context, can retrieve their own seller account record and see the approval status as pending. Confirm the response is limited to the current seller’s own account, includes the linked seller profile information required for storefront display, and keeps the rejection reason null while the account is awaiting approval. This validates the seller dashboard status page for a newly onboarded merchant.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller with a newly created account so the request can be executed in the correct seller context.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_pending_status_view

scenario.draft: Verify that an approved seller can sign in and read their own seller account record successfully. Confirm the response shows approved status, preserves the linked seller profile data, and does not expose a rejection reason for an approved account. This scenario validates the account-status information shown after approval when the seller accesses the seller account page using an existing account session.

dependencies.purpose: Create the seller account before authentication so the test can use an existing merchant identity.
Sign in with the same seller credentials to obtain an authenticated seller session before calling the target endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_approved_profile_view

scenario.draft: Verify that a rejected seller can sign in and retrieve their own account record with the rejection outcome visible. Confirm the response shows rejected status, includes the stored rejection reason, and remains scoped to the authenticated seller only. This validates the seller-facing explanation of review outcomes so a rejected merchant can understand why access was denied and whether a resubmission may be needed later.

dependencies.purpose: Create the seller account before authentication so the test can use a real seller identity that has been reviewed.
Sign in with the same seller credentials to establish the seller session required for reading the account status and rejection details.

functions.name: test_api_seller_account_rejected_reason_view

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve an existing seller profile and see the current public storefront identity used across product listings, seller profile pages, and order-history references. Validate that the response contains the seller profile id, the linked seller account summary, shop name, shop description, logo image URI (including the null case when no logo is configured), and current timestamps. Confirm the endpoint is read-only by checking that it returns only the live seller profile data and does not expose historical snapshots or any edit-specific metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because storefront seller-profile viewing requires customer access.

functions.name: test_api_seller_profile_customer_view_current_profile

scenario.draft: Verify how the endpoint behaves when a customer requests a seller profile that is no longer available because the seller account or profile has been deleted or otherwise removed from active exposure. The system should treat the profile as unavailable for customer viewing, return a not-found style outcome, and avoid recreating or substituting a replacement profile. Confirm that no historical snapshot data is exposed through this live profile endpoint and that the response aligns with the platform rule that missing seller profiles are handled as unavailable rather than implicitly restored.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the endpoint is customer-visible and requires a signed-in shopper context.

functions.name: test_api_seller_profile_customer_missing_profile_unavailable

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can retrieve an existing seller profile by sellerProfileId and receive the current live storefront profile only. Validate that the response includes the seller profile id, nested seller account summary, shop name, shop description, logo image URI, createdAt, updatedAt, and deletedAt fields. Confirm that the nested seller account summary exposes the seller account moderation state needed for governance review, and that the endpoint does not return historical snapshot data or create any new snapshot as a side effect. This scenario should focus on the business-visible correctness of the storefront identity data returned by the read operation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator so the role-restricted seller profile read can be executed under the correct permission context.

functions.name: test_api_seller_profile_retrieve_current_profile

scenario.draft: Verify that when an administrator requests a seller profile that cannot be found, the API responds with a not-found outcome and does not expose any profile or account data. The test should confirm the endpoint behaves as a pure read operation, with no updates to seller profile state and no snapshot creation. This covers the business case where the requested storefront identity record is absent or no longer available under the platform's access policy.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator so the role-restricted seller profile read can be executed under the correct permission context.

functions.name: test_api_seller_profile_not_found

scenario.draft: Verify that the administrator-facing seller profile read respects the platform's visibility rules when the seller profile belongs to a seller account whose current lifecycle state makes the profile unavailable. The response should either expose the live profile when allowed or return a not-found or forbidden outcome consistent with access policy, while still avoiding any mutation of seller profile data. This scenario ensures the business rule that public storefront identity is only disclosed when the platform considers the seller profile accessible under current account-state restrictions.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator so the role-restricted seller profile read can be executed under the correct permission context.

functions.name: test_api_seller_profile_access_policy_restriction

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can browse the active category catalog and receive a paginated list of categories with their names, descriptions, and direct subcategories where applicable. The response should reflect the administrator-managed taxonomy in a stable browse order suitable for storefront navigation. Validate that root categories are returned with no parent category reference, while subcategories are represented only one level deep and do not include any deeper nesting. Confirm the response shape matches the paginated category summary collection expected by customer browsing flows.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because this browsing endpoint requires customer authorization before access to the marketplace taxonomy.

functions.name: test_api_customer_category_browsing_active_taxonomy

scenario.draft: Verify that deleted categories are excluded from the customer-facing category browse results. Prepare a catalog state containing both active and soft-deleted categories, then browse the category list as an authenticated customer and confirm only active categories appear. Ensure deleted categories are not shown in the top-level list and are not exposed through any customer-visible nested taxonomy returned by the endpoint. Also confirm that the customer can still browse the remaining active categories normally and that the response remains usable for storefront navigation even when some categories have been removed.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because category browsing is restricted to signed-in customers.

functions.name: test_api_customer_category_browsing_excludes_deleted_categories

scenario.draft: Verify that customer category browsing preserves the platform's one-level hierarchy rule. Prepare categories that include root categories with direct subcategories, then browse the category list as an authenticated customer and confirm the API exposes only direct child categories beneath each parent. Validate that no category is returned with deeper nested descendants and that the browsing response does not flatten or misrepresent the structure. This scenario should confirm the endpoint is suitable for category navigation while preventing exposure of unsupported deeper taxonomy levels.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the category browsing endpoint requires customer access.

functions.name: test_api_customer_category_browsing_one_level_hierarchy

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can create a new top-level marketplace category with a name and description. Confirm the response returns the created category with a generated UUID, the same name and description that were submitted, a null parentCategoryId, a null parentCategory reference, an empty direct subcategory collection, and creation/update timestamps. Also verify the new category is available for browsing as an administrator-managed taxonomy node and does not alter existing products.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as an administrator because this category creation endpoint is restricted to the administrator role.

functions.name: test_api_category_create_top_level

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can create a direct subcategory under an existing top-level category. Use a pre-seeded existing parent category from test data, submit the new child category with that parent reference, and confirm the response shows the child linked to the correct parent while preserving the one-level category hierarchy. Validate that the returned entity exposes the parent summary reference and that the parent category remains unchanged except for now having the new direct child in its category tree.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as an administrator because this category creation endpoint is restricted to the administrator role.

functions.name: test_api_category_create_direct_subcategory

scenario.draft: Verify that category creation is rejected when the requested parent relationship would create a category deeper than one level. Use an authenticated administrator, an existing top-level category, and an existing direct subcategory already present in the seeded dataset, then attempt to create a new category under that subcategory. Confirm the platform does not create any new category record and the existing category hierarchy remains unchanged after the rejected request.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as an administrator because this category creation endpoint is restricted to the administrator role.

functions.name: test_api_category_create_third_level_rejected

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve an active browseable category by categoryId and receive the full category record needed for category detail browsing. The test should confirm the response exposes the category's identity and display data, including name and description, and preserves the one-level taxonomy by showing only the immediate parentCategory and direct subcategory context where applicable. Validate that the category details align with customer browsing expectations and do not imply deeper nesting or unrelated product data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account so the request can be executed with the required customer authorization context.

functions.name: test_api_customer_category_detail_retrieval

scenario.draft: Verify that a category which has been soft-deleted is excluded from customer-facing category detail browsing. The test should attempt to retrieve the deleted category through the customer endpoint and confirm the service responds with a not-found result or equivalent customer-visible absence behavior instead of returning deleted catalog data. This covers the browsing rule that deleted categories are hidden from customer category views even though the underlying record may still exist for administration purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account so the request can be executed with the required customer authorization context.

functions.name: test_api_customer_category_deleted_not_visible

scenario.draft: Verify that requesting a categoryId that does not correspond to any existing category returns a not-found response. The test should confirm the endpoint does not leak unrelated category data, does not fabricate hierarchy information, and keeps the absence behavior consistent for unknown identifiers. This validates the core lookup behavior for customer category browsing when the requested category cannot be found.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account so the request can be executed with the required customer authorization context.

functions.name: test_api_customer_category_not_found

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can update an existing category's display name and description successfully. Create or identify an existing category, then submit a request that changes only the category name and description while leaving the parentCategoryId unchanged. Assert that the response returns the same category ID with the updated name/description, preserves the existing parent linkage and child structure, and keeps the category available in administrator and customer browsing views after the update.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because only administrators can manage categories.

functions.name: test_api_category_update_name_description

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can move a top-level category under another top-level category when the resulting taxonomy still respects the one-level nesting rule. Prepare two existing root categories, then update the target category's parentCategoryId to the new parent category. Assert that the response shows the new parent relationship, the category remains directly accessible as a subcategory of the chosen parent, and sibling categories are unaffected.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because hierarchy changes are restricted to administrators.

functions.name: test_api_category_reparent_to_valid_parent

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator cannot update a category in a way that would create deeper nesting or otherwise break the platform's one-level category structure. Use an existing subcategory as the target and attempt to assign it beneath another subcategory so the resulting hierarchy would be two levels deep. Assert that the update is rejected, the existing parent-child relationships remain unchanged, and the category list/browse structure is not altered by the failed request.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because only administrators can edit category hierarchy.

functions.name: test_api_category_update_reject_deep_nesting

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can delete an existing category and that the deletion removes the category from marketplace taxonomy without affecting unrelated categories. The test should confirm the endpoint returns success, the deleted category is no longer visible in customer category browsing, and browsing the category tree remains stable for other categories and subcategories. This is the primary happy-path business workflow for category removal.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before performing category management actions.

functions.name: test_api_category_delete_success

scenario.draft: Verify that deleting a category which still has products assigned does not delete those products or break product visibility. After the administrator deletes the category, confirm the affected products remain accessible through product search and product detail flows, but are now uncategorized instead of being removed from the marketplace. Also verify that product records, variants, orders, reviews, and preserved snapshots are not deleted as part of the category deletion. This scenario validates the core preservation rule for products tied to a removed category.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before deleting a category that is associated with products.

functions.name: test_api_category_delete_preserves_assigned_products

scenario.draft: Verify the business failure behavior when an administrator attempts to delete a category that cannot be removed because it is missing or structurally protected by category hierarchy rules. The test should confirm the request is rejected without changing the category tree, and that no unrelated categories or product classifications are altered. This scenario covers the important unavailable-category and structural-constraint cases without testing input validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator before attempting to delete a category that is unavailable or structurally protected.

functions.name: test_api_category_delete_missing_or_protected_category

Confirm the response does not expose full product detail, variant trees, or snapshot history, and that products from other categories are not included.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because this category product listing endpoint is customer-protected and requires a valid customer session.

Use a populated category and verify that the returned page changes according to keyword search, minimum and maximum price, in-stock-only behavior, and the selected sort mode such as newest-first or price ascending/descending. Validate that pagination metadata matches the filtered result set and that only matching category products are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because browsing category products is restricted to signed-in customers.

functions.name: test_api_customer_category_products_filtered_browse

scenario.draft: Test the category browsing visibility rules for edge cases. Confirm that products with no available variants still appear in the category listing but are represented as unavailable rather than removed. Confirm that deleted products and products owned by suspended sellers do not appear in category browse results. Also confirm that deleted categories are excluded from browsing and that a non-browsable category returns the appropriate not-found or access-related response instead of a product list.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer because the endpoint requires customer authorization before category browsing can be evaluated.

functions.name: test_api_customer_category_products_visibility_rules

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can create a direct subcategory under an existing top-level category. Assert that the response returns the newly created category with the expected fields, including a non-null parentCategoryId pointing to the supplied parent, and that the new category is visible as a direct child when browsing the parent category's subcategories. Also confirm that the created category remains only one level deep and does not introduce any deeper nesting.

Create the parent top-level category that will own the new direct subcategory.

Use that child category's identifier as the parent path parameter for a second subcategory creation attempt. Assert that the system rejects the request because it would create a second nesting level, and confirm the existing category hierarchy remains unchanged with only one parent-to-child relationship.

Create the parent top-level category needed to establish a valid direct child hierarchy first.

Also confirm no unrelated sibling categories are modified.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because category management is restricted to administrator users.

functions.name: test_api_category_subcategory_update_success

Confirm the system rejects the change, preserves the existing taxonomy, and leaves both the target subcategory and its siblings unchanged. This scenario should focus on the one-level nesting rule and sibling-name uniqueness under the same parent category.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an administrator because only administrators may manage categories and subcategories.

functions.name: test_api_category_subcategory_update_taxonomy_rule_rejected

scenario.draft: Verify that the endpoint only updates a subcategory when it is actually scoped under the parent category specified in the path. Confirm the operation fails to apply any change because the subcategory is not under the requested parent scope, and verify the original category structure remains unchanged in both branches. This protects administrators from editing the wrong taxonomy branch.

scenario.draft: Test the primary customer-facing catalog browse flow for marketplace products. Confirm that the response excludes soft-deleted or otherwise unavailable products and that pagination metadata is correct for the requested page and limit. functions.name: test_api_product_browse_category_price_stock_sorting

functions.name: test_api_product_browse_missing_category

Validate the response includes the product identity, owning seller summary, category summary when assigned, name, description, base price, and lifecycle timestamps. Confirm the returned seller and category objects are populated consistently with the product and that the operation does not modify any state, create snapshots, or affect inventory, cart, or wishlist data.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_retrieve_active_product

scenario.draft: Test the browse-visibility rule for a product that exists but is not available to customers, such as a soft-deleted product or a product hidden by platform rules. Verify the endpoint remains read-only and does not create snapshots, update inventory history, or mutate any related marketplace data. This confirms the product detail lookup only succeeds for an actual stored product record.

functions.name: test_api_product_detail_not_found_for_missing_product

functions.name: test_api_product_creation_by_approved_seller

Also confirm that all other cart items are preserved exactly as they were and that the returned cart page can be used to redraw the cart immediately.

The refreshed cart should still represent the customer's current cart state after the rejected mutation attempt, demonstrating that the operation is transactional and preserves unchanged lines.

Also verify the cart's updated timestamp changes as part of the successful mutation.

instruction:
Implement the API functions for the e-commerce shopping mall platform based on the completed analysis, database schema, interface specification, and tests. Follow the requirements exactly as provided in the conversation history.

Key behaviors to implement:
- Customer and seller authentication/account lifecycle
- Customer profile and address management
- Seller profile management with snapshots on every edit
- Category browsing and admin-only category management
- Product CRUD with snapshots, images, and variant management
- Variant inventory history and current stock calculation
- Product search, listing, detail, wishlist, and cart operations
- Checkout flow with address selection, payment success/failure handling, order creation, cart item removal, and stock deduction
- Order listing/detail/history and derived order status logic
- Shipping creation by seller, shipment tracking, delivery confirmation, and 14-day auto-delivery behavior
- Cancellation and refund request creation, approval/rejection, snapshot creation, stock restoration, and order status updates
- Review creation/edit/delete with snapshots and product rating aggregation
- Seller dashboard summaries and order-item filtering
- Administrator approval flows, grade promotion/demotion, seller/customer banning, suspending/unsuspending sellers, product/order oversight, and force cancel/refund actions
- Preserve snapshots and historical order data after customer/seller deletion
- Enforce all business-rule constraints, especially deletion restrictions, status restrictions, request windows, and visibility rules

Implementation expectations:
- Use TypeScript + NestJS service/provider patterns
- Ensure business rules are enforced server-side
- Keep code consistent with the generated interface layer and Prisma/database model
- Prefer transactional operations where stock/order state/snapshot integrity matters
- Include robust validation and guard clauses
- Preserve immutable snapshots and historical records exactly as specified
